Head of Communications
Lead external communications for Nuro as its autonomous-driving platform moves deeper into partner-led commercialization.
What the role actually is
Nuro is hiring a Head of Communications to shape the company's external voice across media, customers, partners, policymakers, and autonomy audiences. The work centers on technical storytelling, major announcements, executive communications, issues response, and clear narratives around self-driving technology.
This is a senior communications role for a company trying to make autonomous driving legible beyond the robotics and AI bubble. The person would need to translate safety, commercialization, and technical platform work into messages that can hold up in public.
What you would work on
Build Nuro's external communications strategy across media, partners, policy, and industry audiences
Turn autonomy, AI, safety, and commercialization work into accurate public narratives
Lead major announcements, technical storytelling, executive prep, and rapid-response communications
Partner with brand, marketing, product, legal, policy, and leadership on public-facing moments
What they are asking for
Communications leadership experience in a technical, mobility, AI, robotics, or high-scrutiny category
Strong writing and editorial judgment for technical and executive audiences
Ability to advise leaders and align teams around disciplined messaging
Comfort explaining complex autonomy concepts without overstating the technology
Why this one is worth a look
Autonomy companies live or die partly on trust. Nuro's shift toward a universal autonomy platform makes communications more than brand polish: the role has to explain what the system can do, where it fits, and why partners and the public should believe it.

Design and UX
Head of Product Design
Lead product design and user research for Shield AI tools across autonomy development, simulation, deployment, and operations.
What the role actually is
Shield AI is hiring a Head of Product Design for its Hivemind Enterprise work. The role blends product design, UX leadership, and user research for technical users working on autonomy development, simulation, testing, deployment, and mission operations.
This is a senior design seat in a defense robotics environment where the interfaces have to make complex autonomous systems understandable to engineers, operators, and mission planners.
What you would work on
Lead customer and user research across product, customer engagement, and solutions teams
Design end-to-end workflows for autonomy development, simulation, analysis, deployment, and operations
Turn operational feedback into product requirements and design initiatives
Create experiences for autonomy engineers, software developers, operators, and mission planners
Build design practices and team capacity around complex AI and robotics tools
What they are asking for
Senior product design, UX design, human factors, or related experience
A record of shipping complex technical products, developer tools, platforms, or data-heavy applications
Experience conducting user research and translating insights into product strategy
Technical fluency with engineering workflows, constraints, and AI-powered products
Comfort leading in ambiguous product spaces where interaction patterns are still being invented
Why this one is worth a look
Robotics design roles often sit downstream of engineering, but this one is explicitly tied to product discovery and workflow definition. The caveat is the defense context: it is high-consequence work, and the best fit is someone who wants to design tools for autonomy teams and operators rather than consumer-facing software.

Humanoid companies live or die by whether their policies survive contact with the real world. This role is worth tracking because it is explicitly about deployed visuomotor manipulation, not just training models in a lab setting.

text:
Human-Robot Interaction Applied Scientist, Fauna — Fauna Robotics — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
User Research
Human-Robot Interaction Applied Scientist, Fauna
Develop conversational and social interaction systems for Fauna's home robotics team.
What the role actually is
Fauna is hiring an applied scientist focused on human-robot interaction for a home robot. The job centers on verbal and non-verbal interaction, conversational behavior, social dynamics, memory, and long-term relationship formation.
The work sits between robotics, large language models, multimodal interaction, and user-facing behavior. It is about making robot responses feel fluid, socially appropriate, and trustworthy in real environments.
What you would work on
Develop HRI systems for conversation, turn-taking, grounding, and interruption handling
Use multimodal signals and physical context to shape robot behavior
Explore RLHF or related feedback methods for social robot interaction
Work with design and robotics teams to turn research into embodied behavior
What they are asking for
Applied science experience in HRI, embodied AI, social robotics, or conversational systems
Ability to reason about both technical model behavior and human perception
Comfort evaluating interactions that unfold over time in physical settings
Experience collaborating with design, research, and robotics engineering partners
Why this one is worth a look
Most robotics jobs optimize task completion. This one is explicitly about the social layer: how a robot behaves around people, remembers context, and avoids feeling brittle or awkward. That makes it highly aligned with The Robot Age's HRI lens.

Fauna Robotics
Amazon-owned robotics team building safe, expressive robots for everyday human spaces.

Human-Robot Interaction Applied Scientist, Fauna
Develop verbal and non-verbal interaction systems for socially intelligent home robots.
What the role actually is
Fauna is hiring an HRI applied scientist in New York to develop interactions that make robots feel socially aware, personal, and trustworthy. The role covers conversation, turn-taking, multimodal input and output, memory, and long-term human-robot relationships.
It sits directly at the intersection of robotics, large language models, social interaction, and user-facing behavior. The work is about what a robot says, how it responds, and how it uses physical context around people.
What you would work on
Build conversational systems for turn-taking, grounding, and interruption handling
Use multimodal robot context to shape social and behavioral responses
Explore feedback-driven methods such as RLHF for embodied interaction
Integrate verbal and non-verbal behavior into trustworthy robot experiences
What they are asking for
Applied science experience in HRI, AI, ML, conversational systems, or related fields
Strong programming ability in Python, C++, Java, or a similar language
Research record through publications, patents, or deployed applied systems
Comfort evaluating interactions between robots and people over time
Why this one is worth a look
This is one of the clearest HRI roles on the market right now. It is not just autonomy or interface work with a robot nearby; the job is explicitly about social behavior, memory, conversation, and embodied trust.

text:
Industrial Designer, Fauna — Fauna Robotics — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
Design and UX
Industrial Designer, Fauna
Turn Fauna's robot exterior design direction into production-ready surfaces, finishes, and CMF decisions.
What the role actually is
Fauna is hiring an industrial designer in New York to work directly in the robot hardware design process. The role focuses on Class A surfacing, cosmetic finish specs, CMF decisions, and the detailed exterior geometry that has to survive tooling and manufacturing.
This is a design role for someone who wants the physical robot itself to be the interface. The work is less about concept decks and more about making exterior parts feel intentional, manufacturable, and trustworthy at product scale.
What you would work on
Own production-intent exterior surfacing for injection-molded robot parts
Translate approved design direction into manufacturable CAD geometry
Partner with design engineers, hardware teams, and vendors on tooling details
Support CMF choices and cosmetic finish specifications for robot surfaces
What they are asking for
Industrial design, design innovation, R&D, manufacturing, or related experience
Ability to manage engineering design projects with CAD-heavy workflows
Comfort working through DFM constraints, tooling conversations, and surface quality
Experience turning physical product details into repeatable production outcomes
Why this one is worth a look
Robotics UX is often treated as software, but people read a robot through its body first. This listing is unusually concrete about exterior geometry, finishes, and production compromises, which makes it a strong fit for designers who care about the robot as a physical product.

Industrial Designer, Fauna
Turn Fauna's robot exterior design direction into production-ready surfaces, finishes, and CMF decisions.
What the role actually is
Fauna is hiring an industrial designer in New York to work directly in the robot hardware design process. The role focuses on Class A surfacing, cosmetic finish specs, CMF decisions, and the detailed exterior geometry that has to survive tooling and manufacturing.
This is a design role for someone who wants the physical robot itself to be the interface. The work is less about concept decks and more about making exterior parts feel intentional, manufacturable, and trustworthy at product scale.
What you would work on
Own production-intent exterior surfacing for injection-molded robot parts
Translate approved design direction into manufacturable CAD geometry
Partner with design engineers, hardware teams, and vendors on tooling details
Support CMF choices and cosmetic finish specifications for robot surfaces
What they are asking for
Industrial design, design innovation, R&D, manufacturing, or related experience
Ability to manage engineering design projects with CAD-heavy workflows
Comfort working through DFM constraints, tooling conversations, and surface quality
Experience turning physical product details into repeatable production outcomes
Why this one is worth a look
Robotics UX is often treated as software, but people read a robot through its body first. This listing is unusually concrete about exterior geometry, finishes, and production compromises, which makes it a strong fit for designers who care about the robot as a physical product.

What the role actually is
Nuro is hiring a lead TPM for the AI Platform organization behind its Level 4 autonomous driving system. The group spans the data flywheel, model training, simulation, evaluation, onboard and offboard systems, cloud services, and fleet tooling.
The role combines TPM team leadership with direct ownership of complex programs that connect autonomy roadmaps to deployment readiness across vehicle platforms and commercial partners.

Surface dependencies, technical blockers, resource constraints, and cross-team tradeoffs
What they are asking for
Technical program leadership experience with AI, autonomy, robotics, or complex software platforms
Ability to manage teams while personally driving difficult cross-functional programs
Strong judgment around technical dependencies, release readiness, testing, and deployment risk
Comfort operating onsite with engineering, product, operations, and partner teams
Why this one is worth a look
This is a program leadership role at the layer where autonomy research becomes a shippable platform. The interesting part is the breadth: data, training, simulation, evaluation, firmware, cloud services, and fleet operations all have to move together before Nuro can deploy its driver across more vehicle programs.

text:
Learning Experience Designer — Applied Intuition — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
Design and UX
Learning Experience Designer
Design learning systems that prepare vehicle operations teams to safely test, operate, maintain, and support autonomous fleets.
What the role actually is
Applied Intuition is hiring a learning experience designer for its Vehicle Operations team in Sunnyvale. The role translates vehicle operations, technical procedures, safety practices, and engineering knowledge into onboarding, training, certification, and performance support.
This is experience design for operators rather than a traditional product surface. The work is about making complex autonomy operations learnable, measurable, and safe for the people who have to execute them.
What you would work on
Design learning programs for onboarding, foundational skills, technical training, and certification
Turn operational, safety, and engineering requirements into practical training experiences
Build instructor-led, hands-on, scenario-based, simulation, assessment, job-aid, and digital learning materials
Use learner feedback, proficiency data, and operational metrics to improve readiness
Explore AI-assisted learning tools for scalable practice, coaching, and content development
What they are asking for
Learning experience, instructional design, technical training, or learning program experience
Strong grounding in adult learning, needs analysis, assessment, and performance-based design
Ability to translate complex technical and operational requirements into usable learning paths
Experience creating e-learning, documentation, presentations, video, and hands-on training
Comfort working with operators, engineers, product teams, safety teams, and subject-matter experts
Why this one is worth a look
Autonomy programs often fail at the operational handoff: people need to know what the system can do, where the limits are, and how to respond under pressure. This role is worth watching because it treats training as part of the robot experience, not as an afterthought.

Applied Intuition
Silicon Valley physical AI company building autonomy, simulation, and operating-system software for vehicles, drones, defense systems, and industrial machines.

Learning Experience Designer
Design learning systems that prepare vehicle operations teams to safely test, operate, maintain, and support autonomous fleets.
What the role actually is
Applied Intuition is hiring a learning experience designer for its Vehicle Operations team in Sunnyvale. The role translates vehicle operations, technical procedures, safety practices, and engineering knowledge into onboarding, training, certification, and performance support.
This is experience design for operators rather than a traditional product surface. The work is about making complex autonomy operations learnable, measurable, and safe for the people who have to execute them.
What you would work on
Design learning programs for onboarding, foundational skills, technical training, and certification
Turn operational, safety, and engineering requirements into practical training experiences
Build instructor-led, hands-on, scenario-based, simulation, assessment, job-aid, and digital learning materials
Use learner feedback, proficiency data, and operational metrics to improve readiness
Explore AI-assisted learning tools for scalable practice, coaching, and content development
What they are asking for
Learning experience, instructional design, technical training, or learning program experience
Strong grounding in adult learning, needs analysis, assessment, and performance-based design
Ability to translate complex technical and operational requirements into usable learning paths
Experience creating e-learning, documentation, presentations, video, and hands-on training
Comfort working with operators, engineers, product teams, safety teams, and subject-matter experts
Why this one is worth a look
Autonomy programs often fail at the operational handoff: people need to know what the system can do, where the limits are, and how to respond under pressure. This role is worth watching because it treats training as part of the robot experience, not as an afterthought.

Collaborate with autonomy teams working across prediction, planning, and evaluation

Interest in translating research into practical autonomy systems
Why this one is worth a look
Generative modeling is moving from media and language into physical decision-making. This Nuro role is a useful marker of how autonomy teams are trying to make learned planners more capable without losing control of safety and evaluation.

Marketing Manager, Audience Growth
Build audience growth strategy across social channels and digital communities for Shield AI's autonomy and aircraft products.
What the role actually is
Shield AI is hiring an audience-growth marketer for first-party social channels and third-party digital communities. The role is about understanding which audiences matter for Shield AI's mission, where they gather, and what content moves them.
The work sits between marketing analytics, communications, paid growth, and product storytelling. It is a useful fit for someone who likes turning channel data into sharper narratives for advanced robotics and defense technology.
What you would work on
Analyze audience growth across LinkedIn, X, Instagram, YouTube, Reddit, and industry communities
Build segmentation frameworks for priority personas, content interests, and channel behavior
Manage paid-growth levers and budget for audience acquisition and engagement
Report on growth, engagement, conversion, retention, and testing results
What they are asking for
Experience in growth marketing, digital analytics, audience development, or social analytics
Ability to translate channel performance data into clear recommendations
Familiarity with paid social, acquisition campaigns, and reporting dashboards
Interest in aerospace, defense, national security, autonomy, or advanced technology
Why this one is worth a look
Audience growth can sound abstract, but for robotics and autonomy companies it shapes which customers, recruits, and policymakers understand the technology early. The caveat is that this is more distribution and analytics than product marketing strategy, so the best fit is a quantitative marketer who still cares about the story.

Analyze audience growth across LinkedIn, X, Instagram, YouTube, Reddit, and industry communities

title: Marketing Manager, Events and Content — Collaborative Robotics — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
text:
Marketing Manager, Events and Content — Collaborative Robotics — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
Marketing
Marketing Manager, Events and Content
Own Cobot's external events, customer demo experiences, and content that makes its humanoid work legible to buyers and partners.
What the role actually is
Collaborative Robotics is hiring a hands-on marketing manager for events and content. The job centers on making physical AI understandable in the moments where people actually see it: trade shows, customer visits, partner meetings, investor demos, and the content that follows.
This is not a generic brand role. The person would coordinate marketing, GTM, engineering, design, and leadership to turn robot demonstrations into clear stories and measurable pipeline.
What you would work on
Plan and execute major external events and selected smaller activations
Shape customer, partner, and investor visits around live robot demonstrations
Draft event recaps, launch copy, technical explainers, and executive social posts
Track event-sourced pipeline, audience growth, engagement, and content performance
What they are asking for
Experience producing events, campaigns, or content in a technical B2B environment
Strong writing and project management across marketing, design, and technical teams
Comfort owning logistics, vendors, budgets, run-of-show, and follow-up
Ability to turn complex robot capabilities into stories non-builders can understand
Why this one is worth a look
Cobot is building humanoid robots, which means the product often has to be believed in person before it is understood. This role sits right at that translation layer: the caveat is that it is onsite and execution-heavy, but the storytelling problem is unusually close to the actual robot.

Collaborative Robotics

Own Dexterity's Physical AI marketing story, translating industrial robotics into credible enterprise demand.

What you would work on
Define Dexterity's Physical AI positioning and messaging
Build content and campaigns that turn technical capabilities into enterprise demand
Translate robotics, world-model, and deployment concepts for operations buyers
Partner with product, growth, sales, and leadership on go-to-market strategy

Senior B2B marketing or product marketing experience for technical enterprise products

Strong commercial judgment around demand generation and buyer education

ML Research Scientist, Prediction and Smart Agents
Research prediction and agent behavior models for Nuro's autonomous driving system.
What the role actually is
Nuro is hiring an ML research scientist for prediction and smart agents. The role appears focused on how autonomous systems model the behavior of other actors and use that understanding to make better driving decisions.
This is an autonomy research job with a strong behavioral component. The work affects how an embodied AI system interprets traffic scenes and responds to human-driven uncertainty.
What you would work on
Develop prediction models and smart-agent approaches for autonomous driving
Evaluate learned behavior models across simulated and real-world scenarios
Work with autonomy teams on planning, prediction, and deployment constraints
Improve how the system reasons about dynamic road users
What they are asking for
Research background in ML, prediction, agents, robotics, or autonomous systems
Experience building and evaluating models for sequential decision-making
Ability to reason about uncertainty in physical environments
Comfort collaborating with production autonomy engineers
Why this one is worth a look
The title is technical, but the problem is deeply interaction-oriented. Prediction work determines whether an autonomous vehicle can behave around people in ways that are smooth, legible, and safe.

Nuro

title: Operations Senior Technical Program Manager — Apptronik — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
text:
Operations Senior Technical Program Manager — Apptronik — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
Product
Operations Senior Technical Program Manager
Represent operations inside Apptronik's engineering programs as Apollo moves from product development into production.
What the role actually is
Apptronik is hiring a senior technical program manager for operations in Austin. The role connects engineering, operations, supply chain, manufacturing, quality, service, finance, and procurement as Apollo moves through prototype and production builds.
This is a product-adjacent program role for humanoid scale-up. The person would make sure engineering decisions account for manufacturability, sourcing, serviceability, quality, and build readiness before they become production problems.
What you would work on
Represent operations inside cross-functional engineering programs from concept through launch
Lead build readiness across prototype, EVT, DVT, PVT, and production phases
Coordinate manufacturing, supply chain, quality, test, service, IT, facilities, and procurement workstreams
Drive early resolution of manufacturability, sourcing, serviceability, and quality risks
What they are asking for
Senior technical program management experience in hardware, robotics, manufacturing, or operations-heavy products
Ability to work across engineering, supply chain, manufacturing, quality, finance, and service teams
Experience turning product-development ambiguity into launch plans, readiness criteria, and ownership
Comfort with an onsite Austin role tied closely to Apptronik's humanoid production work
Why this one is worth a look
Humanoid robotics has a very real product gap between a working prototype and a machine that can be built, serviced, and supported repeatedly. This role sits in that gap, so it is a good fit for someone who likes the operational reality of shipping robots more than pure roadmap work.

title: Perception Engineer - Multimodal and Embodied AI — Shield AI — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
text:
Perception Engineer - Multimodal and Embodied AI — Shield AI — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
User Research
Perception Engineer - Multimodal and Embodied AI
Turn multimodal vision, foundation-model, and embodied-AI research into perception capabilities for autonomous aircraft.
What the role actually is
Shield AI is hiring a perception engineer to move promising AI research into real autonomous systems. The role evaluates multimodal computer vision, visual foundation models, and embodied AI methods, then turns the useful pieces into Hivemind perception capabilities.
This is a research-to-product role: experiments and prototypes matter, but so do sensor constraints, edge deployment, testing, documentation, and adoption by autonomy teams.
What you would work on
Evaluate emerging perception and embodied-AI methods against representative autonomy data
Build prototypes that expose where models work, fail, and can be deployed
Combine learned and classical approaches for detection, tracking, geometric vision, or sensor fusion
Optimize and integrate perception capabilities for edge robotics systems
Carry successful experiments into tested Hivemind capabilities that other teams can adopt
What they are asking for
Research depth in computer vision, robotics, machine learning, or embodied learning
Experience with multimodal vision, visual foundation models, video understanding, or open-vocabulary perception
Strong Python skills and practical work with PyTorch or a similar machine learning framework
Ability to design careful experiments, understand model failures, and build substantial research software
Interest in production-quality C++ and collaboration with product engineering teams
Why this one is worth a look
This is one of the cleaner bridges between the current foundation-model wave and deployed robotics. The caveat is that it sits inside defense autonomy, but the technical problem is exactly the one many robot companies are wrestling with: making general AI perception useful on real hardware under real constraints.

Shield AI

title: Presentation Designer — Shield AI — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
text:
Presentation Designer — Shield AI — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
Design and UX
Presentation Designer
Turn Shield AI's autonomy, aircraft, and simulation concepts into clear executive and customer-facing presentation systems.
What the role actually is
Shield AI is hiring a presentation designer in Washington, D.C. to create high-impact decks and reusable presentation systems for complex defense autonomy products. The work sits with marketing and business development, but the day-to-day design problem is information design for technical systems.
The role is about making product, engineering, and mission concepts legible in slides without flattening the details that matter.
What you would work on
Design polished presentation decks from rough outlines, sketches, and stakeholder input
Build slide templates, libraries, product decks, sales decks, and executive materials
Translate technical diagrams, workflows, data, and system concepts into clear visuals
Partner with marketing, product marketing, business development, and solutions engineering
Maintain visual hierarchy, data integrity, and reusable presentation components
What they are asking for
Strong information-design judgment for quantitative, technical, and conceptual material
Experience building PowerPoint templates, slide libraries, and flagship product or sales decks
Ability to simplify complex systems without distorting the underlying meaning
Skill with charts, process flows, system diagrams, timelines, and presentation graphics
Familiarity with tools such as Figma, Illustrator, or Photoshop
Why this one is worth a look
This is not a classic robotics UX role, but it belongs on the board because technical storytelling is part of how autonomous systems get understood, bought, and deployed. It is a narrower design role than product design, with more focus on executive and customer communication than interface ownership.

The role is about making product, engineering, and mission concepts legible in slides without flattening the details that matter.
What you would work on
Design polished presentation decks from rough outlines, sketches, and stakeholder input
Build slide templates, libraries, product decks, sales decks, and executive materials
Translate technical diagrams, workflows, data, and system concepts into clear visuals
Partner with marketing, product marketing, business development, and solutions engineering
Maintain visual hierarchy, data integrity, and reusable presentation components
What they are asking for
Strong information-design judgment for quantitative, technical, and conceptual material
Experience building PowerPoint templates, slide libraries, and flagship product or sales decks
Ability to simplify complex systems without distorting the underlying meaning
Skill with charts, process flows, system diagrams, timelines, and presentation graphics
Familiarity with tools such as Figma, Illustrator, or Photoshop
Why this one is worth a look
This is not a classic robotics UX role, but it belongs on the board because technical storytelling is part of how autonomous systems get understood, bought, and deployed. It is a narrower design role than product design, with more focus on executive and customer communication than interface ownership.

text:
Principal Product Manager - Atlas Logistics Robotics — Boston Dynamics — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
Product
Principal Product Manager - Atlas Logistics Robotics
Define product strategy and customer workflows for Atlas logistics robotics deployments.
What the role actually is
Boston Dynamics is hiring a principal product manager in Waltham for Atlas logistics robotics. The role defines product strategy for humanoid logistics automation, translating warehouse customer workflows, pain points, and deployment criteria into product roadmaps and requirements.
This is a senior product role at the point where Atlas has to become a usable logistics product, not just an impressive robotics platform.
What you would work on
Build business plans and roadmaps for Atlas logistics solutions
Lead product discovery with logistics customers, prospects, and strategic partners
Turn warehouse workflows, market gaps, and customer needs into product artifacts and roadmap tradeoffs
Partner with hardware, software, AI, and go-to-market teams on humanoid logistics applications
Own product lifecycle work from customer engagement and business cases through prioritization, development, and launch
What they are asking for
Senior product management experience or equivalent industry experience
Ability to create long-term product vision while keeping an executable roadmap for engineering teams
Experience translating customer processes into requirements for end-to-end robotics solutions
Comfort working with software and hardware engineering teams in ambiguous environments
Logistics, warehousing, fulfillment, robotics, or new technology introduction experience
Why this one is worth a look
Atlas product management is a high-signal role because the core question is practical: what does a humanoid have to do for large logistics customers before it becomes a product they can buy and deploy? The caveat is the seniority and travel: Boston Dynamics expects a customer-facing product leader who can work from warehouse-floor details up to executive strategy.

title: Probabilistic Risk Assessment Engineer — Kodiak — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
text:
Probabilistic Risk Assessment Engineer — Kodiak — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
User Research
Probabilistic Risk Assessment Engineer
Build probabilistic risk models and validation methods for Kodiak's autonomous trucking safety case.
What the role actually is
Kodiak is hiring a probabilistic risk assessment engineer for its Autonomy Safety team. The role focuses on estimating and reducing risk in autonomous trucking through Bayesian models, simulations, hazard analysis, fault trees, and validation strategy.
For this board, the relevance is the evaluation layer: the work shapes how a deployed autonomous vehicle company proves that its system is safe enough to operate.
What you would work on
Estimate autonomy risk using Bayesian probabilistic models
Search for failure modes in high-dimensional autonomy scenarios
Run simulations and analyses that inform engineering priorities
Perform hazard analysis, fault tree analysis, and structured risk assessment
Help define validation strategies for autonomous truck safety
What they are asking for
Deep systems thinking for autonomy safety and risk assessment
Strong mathematical grounding in probability, modeling, or related analysis
Ability to use Python, C++, simulation, and data analysis to reason about rare but severe failures
Experience connecting safety analysis to engineering decisions and validation plans
Comfort working on an open-ended safety problem without a simple textbook answer
Why this one is worth a look
Safety roles can become process-heavy, but this one is framed as a frontier modeling and evaluation problem. Kodiak is asking how to quantify and prove safety for autonomous trucks in the real world, which makes the work unusually central to whether the product can scale.

Kodiak
Mountain View autonomous trucking company building self-driving software for commercial freight and public-sector ground vehicles.

Probabilistic Risk Assessment Engineer
Build probabilistic risk models and validation methods for Kodiak's autonomous trucking safety case.
What the role actually is
Kodiak is hiring a probabilistic risk assessment engineer for its Autonomy Safety team. The role focuses on estimating and reducing risk in autonomous trucking through Bayesian models, simulations, hazard analysis, fault trees, and validation strategy.
For this board, the relevance is the evaluation layer: the work shapes how a deployed autonomous vehicle company proves that its system is safe enough to operate.
What you would work on
Estimate autonomy risk using Bayesian probabilistic models
Search for failure modes in high-dimensional autonomy scenarios
Run simulations and analyses that inform engineering priorities
Perform hazard analysis, fault tree analysis, and structured risk assessment
Help define validation strategies for autonomous truck safety
What they are asking for
Deep systems thinking for autonomy safety and risk assessment
Strong mathematical grounding in probability, modeling, or related analysis
Ability to use Python, C++, simulation, and data analysis to reason about rare but severe failures
Experience connecting safety analysis to engineering decisions and validation plans
Comfort working on an open-ended safety problem without a simple textbook answer
Why this one is worth a look
Safety roles can become process-heavy, but this one is framed as a frontier modeling and evaluation problem. Kodiak is asking how to quantify and prove safety for autonomous trucks in the real world, which makes the work unusually central to whether the product can scale.

Product Design Engineer (All Levels)
Design mechanical parts, assemblies, and production-ready hardware for Skydio's autonomous drones and accessories.
What the role actually is
Skydio is hiring a product design engineer in San Mateo to develop the mechanical systems behind its autonomous drones, ground stations, and accessories. The work sits in R&D and runs from early architecture through prototyping, testing, vendor work, and production support.
This is physical product design rather than digital UX. It still belongs on the board because the role shapes the drone hardware that operators hold, deploy, inspect, and trust in the field.
What you would work on
Design mechanical parts and assemblies for aircraft, ground stations, and accessories
Integrate structures, mechanisms, antennas, cable harnesses, and custom electronics into drone hardware
Define tests and use analysis to compare design tradeoffs
Work with vendors, operations, supply chain, manufacturing, and factory teams
Debug failures and carry designs from prototype into pre-production and mass production
What they are asking for
Product development experience with mechanical systems
Mechanical engineering fundamentals and strong analytical problem-solving skills
Advanced 3D CAD experience, with CATIA preferred
Familiarity with manufacturing processes such as injection molding, casting, CNC machining, sheet metal, or composites
Comfort prototyping quickly while producing production-quality drawings and documentation
Why this one is worth a look
Skydio's autonomy is only useful if the aircraft and accessories survive field use. This role is a good fit for someone who wants product design work that is tactile, technical, and close to deployed drone systems instead of purely screen-based design.

text:
Product Designer, Defense — Applied Intuition — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
Design and UX
Product Designer, Defense
Own defense product design across real-time operator interfaces and enterprise tools for autonomy programs.
What the role actually is
Applied Intuition is hiring a product designer for its defense product surface. The role spans real-time command, control, and situational awareness interfaces as well as enterprise web tools used by defense engineering teams and customers.
This is a high-context autonomy design role. The work is about helping operators, engineers, and partners understand what the system is doing, where it needs human approval, and how autonomy moves from bespoke program work into repeatable products.
What you would work on
Own end-to-end design for one or more defense products, from research through shipped UI
Design operator interfaces for tablets, ground stations, shipboard systems, and airborne environments
Build approval and escalation patterns for agentic autonomy where humans stay meaningfully in the loop
Extend a defense design system across real-time and enterprise workflows
Support demos, program reviews, and customer-facing design conversations
What they are asking for
Product, tools, interaction, or systems design experience in complex technical products
Strong visual and interaction design craft with an ability to learn defense context quickly
Comfort conducting primary research with operators, analysts, engineers, and partners
Ability to prototype clearly and work closely with PM and engineering teams
Willingness to travel to bases, ranges, customer sites, and related field contexts
Why this one is worth a look
This is one of the more direct "robot UX under pressure" roles on the market. The design problem is not just dashboard polish; it is trust, timing, constrained connectivity, and the question of when an autonomous system should ask a person to decide.

Product Designer, HMI
Design production-grade human-machine interfaces for future vehicle and autonomy products at Applied Intuition.
What the role actually is
Applied Intuition is hiring a product designer focused on human-machine interfaces for future vehicles. The role owns design direction for a strategically important HMI project, moving from early concepts to production-quality interface work.
This is a robotics-adjacent design job where the interface has to make vehicle state, controls, and autonomy behavior understandable. The designer will need to work closely with product, engineering, and stakeholders while carrying end-to-end ownership of the visual and interaction system.

Lead HMI design from concept explorations through production-ready product surfaces
Create flows, prototypes, and interface systems for vehicle and autonomy experiences

Product Designer, Manufacturing and Defense
Design factory-floor and customer workflows for robotic NDT data collection and critical manufacturing decisions.
What the role actually is
Gecko is hiring a product designer for manufacturing and defense workflows built around robotic non-destructive testing systems and the software that turns inspection data into decisions. The role combines user research, product strategy, product design, and frequent customer-site work.
This is a good fit for the board because the design surface is tied to robots in industrial environments, not just reporting software. The designer has to understand operators, engineers, customers, and the quality constraints around safety-critical components.
What you would work on
Design workflows for human-operated and autonomous robotic NDT data collection
Work with users at plants, forges, shops, and other customer sites
Translate material-health data and factory constraints into usable product flows
Partner with robotics teams, strategists, engineers, field operators, and customers
What they are asking for
Product design experience in ambiguous, technical, or industrial product environments
Strong user-centered research habits and comfort working directly with customers
Ability to define what is worth building, not only how a feature looks
Eligibility for work that may involve controlled U.S. government information
Why this one is worth a look
Gecko's product challenge is making complex robotic inspection legible to people making high-stakes manufacturing and defense decisions. The valuable design work is in the translation layer between physical data capture, factory reality, and operational judgment.

Gecko Robotics
Pittsburgh robotics company using wall-climbing robots and AI to inspect and maintain critical infrastructure.

text:

Product Designer
Become Treeswift's first full-time designer across geospatial software, hardware interfaces, and utility field workflows.
What the role actually is
Treeswift is hiring its first full-time product designer. The company builds physical AI for utility field work, using hardware, sensing, AI, and software to help teams inspect, triage, and act on field data.
The role owns end-to-end product design across the web platform and hardware physical interfaces. The core design challenge is making geospatial, imagery, LiDAR, and operational data usable for arborists, storm responders, and utility operations teams.
What you would work on
Own product design from discovery and workflow mapping through prototypes, implementation details, and iteration
Design interfaces for dense field data, including maps, imagery, LiDAR, and utility operations context
Build Treeswift's design system, component library, interaction patterns, and visual language
Turn customer-specific workflows into reusable product primitives
Work closely with product, engineering, deployed teams, customer teams, and sales
What they are asking for
Product design experience shipping complex B2B or enterprise software
Strong interaction design, information design, and visual design craft
Comfort operating as both a senior IC and design-function builder
Ability to work through ambiguity in an early-stage environment
Experience with design systems; geospatial or map-heavy work is a plus
Why this one is worth a look
This is a classic first-designer robotics role: messy field data, real operational users, and a chance to set the patterns before the product hardens. The caveat is the same as the appeal: it will likely require comfort with ambiguity and a lot of hands-on systems building.

Treeswift
New York physical AI company building field-work software and sensing systems for utilities, vegetation management, and infrastructure operations.

Product Lead, Marketplace Pricing — Zipline — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
Product
Product Lead, Marketplace Pricing
Shape the marketplace pricing systems and operational economics behind Zipline's autonomous delivery network.
What the role actually is
Zipline is hiring an individual-contributor product lead to work on the marketplace economics behind its drone delivery network. The role connects engineering, design, operations, commercial teams, and customer experience around pricing, dispatch logic, supply and demand systems, data, and operator workflows.
The posting is less about a conventional SaaS surface and more about product decisions that affect real-world delivery execution at scale.
What you would work on
Identify user pain points and operational inefficiencies in Zipline's delivery marketplace

What the role actually is
Shield AI is hiring a product manager for AI/ML and foundation models inside its Hivemind autonomy platform. The role owns the workflows and product requirements around training pipelines, data infrastructure, synthetic data, model evaluation, governance, and deployment onto edge autonomy systems.

Product management experience for technical ML, AI, or data infrastructure products

Product Manager
Own platform and vertical product work for Dana, Applied Intuition's agentic platform for physical AI development.
What the role actually is
Applied Intuition is hiring a product manager for Dana, its platform for building agents, apps, and data workflows for physical AI. The role owns shared platform capabilities while also driving hands-on product execution for one or more autonomy verticals.
This is a technical product role for someone who can work with autonomy customers, internal engineering teams, design, TPMs, and go-to-market partners.
What you would work on
Define what Dana should build from customer use cases, market needs, and business goals
Decide which capabilities should be platform-wide versus tailored to specific autonomy verticals
Partner with engineering and design on product direction, tradeoffs, prioritization, and release work
Present capabilities to customers, gather feedback, and turn field learning into roadmap decisions
Support positioning, launch material, pricing, and customer engagement with sales and marketing
What they are asking for
Product management experience in a technical company or high-growth startup
Ability to build trust across engineering and learn complex autonomy workflows quickly
Technical fluency with software products, platform decisions, and customer-facing tradeoffs
Comfort owning product direction in a high-visibility, fast-moving environment
Why this one is worth a look
Dana sits in the tooling layer around physical AI rather than a single robot program. That makes the role interesting for product people who want leverage across cars, trucks, mining, and other autonomy domains, while still staying close to real customer workflows.

title: Product Manager - DefenseOS — Applied Intuition — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
text:
Product Manager - DefenseOS — Applied Intuition — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
Product
Product Manager - DefenseOS
Own the product strategy for DefenseOS as Applied adapts its VehicleOS work to unmanned and traditional naval platforms.
What the role actually is
Applied Intuition is hiring a product manager for DefenseOS, a defense operating-system product derived from its commercial VehicleOS work. The first focus is a naval surface-vessel operating system that integrates combat, communications, hull, mechanical, and electrical systems.
This is an IC product role with direct customer discovery, roadmap ownership, and close partnership with engineering, design, and operations.
What you would work on
Own the DefenseOS product vision, strategy, and roadmap
Translate Navy program office, operator, and crew needs into product requirements
Shape how a zonal architecture integrates with existing defense systems and legacy interfaces
Sequence field readiness, adoption, and product scope with engineering and operations partners
Drive product outcomes through influence rather than direct management
What they are asking for
Product management experience with complex technical systems
Ability to work with defense customers, operators, and engineering teams
Strong judgment around requirements, prioritization, and roadmap tradeoffs
Comfort with architecture-heavy software products that interface with real hardware systems
Why this one is worth a look
This is a product job at the edge of commercial autonomy software and defense modernization. The caveat is obvious: it is defense work, but for someone interested in unmanned maritime systems, the scope is unusually direct.

Product Manager - Developer Tooling
Own developer-tooling products for Applied Intuition's autonomous-vehicle software customers.
What the role actually is
Applied Intuition is hiring a product manager for developer tooling inside its Vehicle OS work. The role owns a product end to end, from strategy and market understanding through engineering execution, launch, customer feedback, and go-to-market support.
This is a technical product role for someone who can bridge autonomy engineers, customers, business development, and marketing.
What you would work on
Define platform products from market understanding, customer use cases, and time-to-market needs
Shape a differentiated value proposition for autonomy developer tools
Partner closely with engineering to prioritize work and ship useful product increments
Manage the product lifecycle from discovery through delivery and business outcome
Work with business development and marketing on pitches, pricing, positioning, and engagement models
What they are asking for
Product management experience in a top technology company or high-growth startup
Experience launching products, ideally involving both software and hardware
Strong technical background and comfort with software development concepts
Ability to own product strategy, execution, customer feedback, and lifecycle management
Why this one is worth a look
Developer tooling is where autonomy products either become easier to build or stay trapped inside bespoke engineering workflows. This role is useful for a PM who wants a software product surface but still wants the constraints of autonomous systems.

Define product priorities for autonomous drone software and edge-compute capabilities
Translate operator, mission, and customer needs into concrete product requirements
Coordinate with engineering on autonomy, platform, and hardware tradeoffs
Support product decisions across multiple airframe vendors and deployment contexts
Help move DroneStack from proven technology into repeatable product delivery
What they are asking for
Product management experience with technical software, defense, robotics, or aerospace systems
Ability to work across customer, operator, engineering, and business constraints
Strong product judgment in ambiguous, fast-moving programs
Comfort with in-office collaboration and complex autonomy topics
Why this one is worth a look
Drone autonomy is becoming less about a single aircraft and more about the stack around many vehicles, missions, and operators. This role is worth watching because it sits at that product layer, where "autonomy" has to become something deployable and usable.

title: Product Manager, Human Robot Interaction — Apptronik — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
text:
Product Manager, Human Robot Interaction — Apptronik — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
Product
Product Manager, Human Robot Interaction
Own the HRI roadmap for Apptronik's Apollo humanoid, translating market needs into robot and interface priorities.
What the role actually is
Apptronik is hiring a product manager for human-robot interaction on Apollo. The role owns roadmap scope, sequencing, and priorities for how the robot and its interfaces create intuitive, positive experiences for people using or working near the system.
This is a classic robotics product role at the hardware/software boundary. The product manager has to turn customer needs, safety constraints, and interaction goals into executable work across teams.
What you would work on
Own and maintain the HRI roadmap for Apollo
Translate market and user needs into product requirements, priorities, and release plans
Shape robot and interface behaviors that make humanoid operation more intuitive
Work across hardware, software, safety, commercialization, and customer-facing teams
What they are asking for
Product management experience with technical, hardware/software, robotics, or AI products
Ability to define product vision and turn ambiguous market needs into executable roadmaps
Comfort collaborating across engineering, design, business, and deployment teams
Strong interest in human-centered robotics and commercial humanoid adoption
Why this one is worth a look
HRI is often treated as a research topic, but Apptronik is hiring it as a product ownership problem. That is the interesting shift: someone has to decide which interaction behaviors ship, in what order, and how they map to real customer use.

text:
Product Manager - Platform — Applied Intuition — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
Product
Product Manager - Platform
Own Dana's core platform experience for building, deploying, sharing, and governing physical AI apps.
What the role actually is
Applied Intuition is hiring a product manager for the core platform behind Dana, its AI platform for physical industries. The role owns the customer-facing builder, deployment, sharing, and governance experience for enterprise users.
This is a platform PM job where product quality, user experience, multi-tenancy, scale, reliability, onboarding, and security review all matter.
What you would work on
Define and ship core capabilities for builders ranging from platform engineers to domain experts
Own product quality and user experience across the Dana platform
Partner with platform engineering on architecture, scale, reliability, and multi-tenant tradeoffs
Work with forward-deployed teams and design partners to understand customer needs
Join enterprise onboarding and security-review conversations when they affect the product
What they are asking for
Product management experience on a cloud or SaaS product shipped to external customers
Ownership of platform capabilities such as integrations, identity, permissions, or hosting
Technical fluency with architecture tradeoffs and multi-tenant systems
Enterprise exposure around security, admin, or IT requirements
Product taste for how the tool feels to the person using it
Why this one is worth a look
This is not a robot-interface role, but it is squarely in the infrastructure that lets physical AI teams build and govern tools. It is a strong fit for PMs who like platform work but want the product context to be machines in the world.

Product
Product Manager - Tech, GO-AI Technology and Development Team
Own GO-AI product strategy for robotics annotation, intervention, data discovery, and foundation-model workflows.
What the role actually is
Amazon Robotics is hiring a technical product manager for the GO-AI Technology and Development team. The role owns roadmap and feature strategy across annotation tools, near-real-time remote intervention, data discovery, reporting, and foundation-model workflows for robotics operations.
The interesting piece is the shift from manual visual reasoning work toward model-assisted automation and teleoperation. This is product management for the systems that help Amazon Robotics scale AI-backed operational decisions.
What you would work on
Define product strategy for GO-AI applications and data workflows
Translate robotics operations needs into roadmap priorities and technical proposals
Shape new capabilities for remote real-time teleoperation
Work with engineering, science, and operations teams on model-assisted annotation and intervention systems
What they are asking for
Product management experience for technical or AI-heavy systems
Ability to work with applied science and engineering teams on architecture tradeoffs
Comfort with robotics, fulfillment operations, annotation, labeling, or foundation-model workflows
Data-driven judgment about customer needs, operations, and product execution
Why this one is worth a look
This role sits at a useful layer of robotics product work: not the robot hardware itself, but the AI operations surface that decides how quickly robots can learn from edge cases and human intervention. It is a strong fit for someone interested in product work around embodied AI infrastructure.

title: Product Manager, Technical Commercialization — Path Robotics — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
text:
Product Manager, Technical Commercialization — Path Robotics — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
Product
Product Manager, Technical Commercialization
Commercialize Path Robotics' AI-driven robotic welding products from technical capability to customer-ready launch.
What the role actually is
Path Robotics is hiring a product manager for technical commercialization. The company builds AI-driven robotic welding systems, and this role is meant to turn complex robotics, AI, and software capabilities into customer-ready products.
The job sits at the zero-to-one product layer: discovery, feasibility, MVP, launch, adoption, and iteration. The listing specifically calls out functional, UX, and system-level requirements for robotic welding cycles and production environments.
What you would work on
Own greenfield product development from early discovery through MVP, commercialization, and launch
Translate robotics, AI, and software capabilities into clear customer value propositions
Define product strategy, success metrics, operating rhythms, and prioritization frameworks
Represent customer needs through research, field insights, and manufacturing workflows
Partner with sales, solutions, and operations on readiness, launch planning, enablement, and adoption
What they are asking for
Experience launching a greenfield product in robotics, manufacturing, automation, AI, or a related technical domain
Technical product management or technical commercialization background
Ability to bridge software, hardware, and data into production-ready solutions
Comfort making decisions from customer insight, usage data, and experimentation
Strong facilitation across engineering, sales, operations, and leadership
Why this one is worth a look
Robotic welding is a useful test of product judgment because the robot has to survive real production constraints. This role is worth watching because it is about turning a hard technical capability into a repeatable commercial product, not just managing an existing roadmap.

Path Robotics
Columbus robotics company building AI-driven robotic welding systems for industrial production environments.

text:
Product Marketing Manager, Defense — Applied Intuition — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
Marketing
Product Marketing Manager, Defense
Lead defense product marketing for Applied Intuition's autonomy, simulation, and physical AI products.
What the role actually is
Applied Intuition is hiring a product marketing manager to own how its defense work is positioned, launched, and understood by the market. The role partners closely with product management and owns messaging, sales enablement, launch programs, and the defense marketing calendar.
This is a marketing role for a technical buyer. The work is about translating autonomy, simulation, and AI-driven product categories into narratives that program offices and senior defense decision-makers can evaluate.
What you would work on
Lead defense marketing strategy across market insights, customer priorities, and product knowledge
Define positioning, naming, messaging, and launch plans for new defense capabilities
Build sales enablement that supports the defense pipeline
Manage marketing objectives, quarterly budgets, and the annual defense marketing calendar
Guide campaign, video, blog, press, social, and event content for defense audiences
What they are asking for
Product marketing experience in software technology, including defense exposure
Ability to translate complex technical ideas into clear product narratives
Strong project management across multiple workstreams
Creative judgment for product, brand, and content development
US citizenship for access to controlled information
Why this one is worth a look
The role sits at the gap between technical autonomy capability and defense adoption. For marketers, that is a serious storytelling challenge: make a complex physical AI platform legible without flattening the hard operational realities that make the category matter.

text:
Product Operations Manager — Kodiak — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
Product
Product Operations Manager
Bridge Kodiak's product, engineering, and field teams so autonomous trucking operations can scale from Lancaster.
What the role actually is
Kodiak is hiring a product operations manager in Lancaster, Texas to connect product and engineering work with field operations. The role owns mechanisms and processes that help the autonomous trucking operation scale.
This is a field-facing product operations job rather than a desk-only product role. The person will need to understand what operators need, how engineering changes land in practice, and where better process design can make autonomous freight deployments more reliable.
What you would work on
Build scalable product operations processes for Kodiak's Lancaster deployment hub
Connect product and engineering teams with operations and field feedback
Design mechanisms that help new operational workflows launch and improve
Track issues, adoption, and process gaps that affect autonomous trucking execution
Help turn deployment lessons into better product and operational decisions
What they are asking for
Product operations, program, or field operations experience in a technical environment
Ability to work closely with engineering, product, and operations teams
Strong process design and execution skills for scaling complex work
Comfort working full-time from Kodiak's Lancaster office
Why this one is worth a look
Autonomous vehicles need strong product operations because field reality changes the roadmap. This role is interesting because it is embedded near the operational footprint, where usability and process failures show up quickly.

Kodiak
Mountain View autonomous trucking company building self-driving software for commercial freight and public-sector ground vehicles.

Product
Product Quality Manager
Drive product-quality plans, issue resolution, and manufacturing readiness as Apptronik scales Apollo.
What the role actually is
Apptronik is hiring a product quality manager for Apollo, its humanoid robot platform. The role documents build and system-test issues, drives corrective action across hardware, operations, and software, and defines product-quality plans as the company moves from prototypes toward production.
This is not a generic quality role. It sits close to product maturity for a humanoid robot that has to move from internal development into repeatable manufacturing and customer-facing reliability.
What you would work on
Lead product-quality processes across builds, system testing, and production readiness
Document issues, align stakeholders, and drive root-cause and corrective action
Build dashboards and visual tools that make top issues visible to leadership
Define quality plans for contract manufacturing and audit adherence
Coordinate quality work across hardware design, operations, software, and manufacturing
What they are asking for
Product quality experience on complex technical or electromechanical products
Ability to lead quality team members and cross-functional issue resolution
Strong critical thinking, ownership, and communication under ambiguity
Experience turning build and test findings into durable process improvements
Comfort working with hardware, software, operations, and manufacturing stakeholders
Why this one is worth a look
Humanoid startups are now hitting the manufacturing and serviceability problems that decide whether a platform becomes a product. Apptronik's role is a useful signal that Apollo's next challenge is not only capability, but product quality at scale.

text:
Product Strategy & Operations Associate — Kodiak — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
Product
Product Strategy & Operations Associate
Turn ambiguous autonomy deployment questions into product, engineering, and operations decisions for Kodiak's self-driving trucks.
What the role actually is
Kodiak is hiring a product strategy and operations associate to work between product, engineering, and operations. The role turns messy questions about how autonomous trucks are built, deployed, and scaled into analyses, recommendations, and operating rhythms.
This is a closer-to-product strategy role rather than a pure business operations job. The person would sit with the teams building the autonomous trucking product and help shape decisions that affect deployment readiness.
What you would work on
Scope ambiguous cross-functional problems into clear analyses and recommendations
Drive product, engineering, and operations decisions from analysis through execution
Build operating cadences, metrics, and dashboards for autonomy deployment work
Help leadership understand tradeoffs across product readiness, field operations, and scale
Turn deployment lessons into clearer process and product priorities
What they are asking for
Strategy, operations, consulting, product operations, or similar analytical experience
Strong structured problem-solving and comfort with ambiguous technical programs
Ability to work closely with product, engineering, and operations leaders
Clear written and verbal communication for decision-making
Interest in getting close to autonomous-vehicle product development
Why this one is worth a look
Kodiak is in the hard middle of autonomy commercialization: not just proving a truck can drive, but deciding what needs to be true for a fleet to scale. This role is interesting because it sits at that product operating layer where field reality turns into roadmap and execution choices.

Kodiak

title: Program Manager — GrayMatter Robotics — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
text:
Program Manager — GrayMatter Robotics — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
Product
Program Manager
Coordinate a multi-year robotic manufacturing facility build for large defense-scale shipbuilding work.
What the role actually is
GrayMatter Robotics is hiring a program manager to act as the continuity point for a large autonomous manufacturing build. The program spans a new facility, multiple robotic applications, an external robotics collaborator, production qualification, and ongoing operations.
The role is product-adjacent program leadership for physical AI at industrial scale. It is less about a software roadmap and more about turning robotic cells, qualification requirements, and customer milestones into one executable plan.
What you would work on
Own delivery across facility setup, robotic applications, qualification, and production ramp
Sequence robotic processes such as cutting, beveling, grinding, blasting, spraying, inspection, and material handling
Coordinate schedules between GrayMatter engineering teams and an external robotics collaborator
Maintain the single source of truth for requirements, milestones, handoffs, and risk
What they are asking for
Experience leading complex industrial, robotics, manufacturing, or defense programs
Ability to manage executive, customer, government, and engineering stakeholders
Comfort translating qualification requirements into a practical delivery roadmap
Willingness to travel to customer and program sites as needed
Why this one is worth a look
This is a rare role where the program manager is effectively holding the whole physical deployment together, from facility readiness to robotic process qualification. The caveat is that the domain is heavy industrial and defense-facing, so it is best for someone who likes hard constraints and long-running execution.

GrayMatter Robotics
Carson robotics company building AI-powered robotic cells for sanding, polishing, and surface finishing.

Product
Program Manager, FMS
Lead Foreign Military Sales program execution for Shield AI's V-BAT work from contract award through delivery and sustainment.
What the role actually is
Shield AI is hiring a program manager for Foreign Military Sales programs tied to its V-BAT business. The role runs execution from contract award through delivery, acceptance, training, sustainment, and follow-on support.
This is a customer-facing program role for deployed autonomous aircraft systems. The person would coordinate government program offices, international customers, engineering, operations, logistics, and sustainment teams.
What you would work on
Lead FMS program execution across delivery, training, fielding, sustainment, and acceptance
Manage U.S. Government and international customer relationships for assigned programs
Track cost, schedule, resource, and performance metrics against contract requirements
Identify bottlenecks and drive critical-path decisions to keep programs on schedule
What they are asking for
Department of Defense program management experience
Ability to manage multiple interrelated projects with limited direction
Familiarity with scheduling tools, complex project financials, and customer reporting
Ability to obtain a Secret security clearance and travel domestically or internationally
Why this one is worth a look
Program roles like this decide whether autonomous systems move from demo to accepted field capability. The caveat is that the work is defense-procurement heavy, but it is close to the real-world adoption loop for robotic aircraft.

title: Program Manager - Growth and Profitability — Zipline — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
text:
Program Manager - Growth and Profitability — Zipline — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
Product
Program Manager - Growth and Profitability
Lead cross-functional growth and profitability programs for Zipline's autonomous delivery network.
What the role actually is
Zipline is hiring a program manager for growth and profitability as its autonomous delivery network scales. The role brings together marketplace strategy, network optimization, product, sales, and marketing work around demand, partner success, and unit economics.
This is not a robotics engineering seat. It is a product and operations program role focused on making autonomous delivery expand in a way that customers, partners, and the business can sustain.
What you would work on
Coordinate Zipline's growth and profitability program across product, sales, marketing, and operations
Help translate partner and customer demand into repeatable growth programs
Work on marketplace strategy, network optimization, and operating economics
Track cross-functional initiatives that improve adoption and partner success
What they are asking for
Program management experience in growth, product operations, marketplace, or strategy work
Ability to coordinate across commercial, product, marketing, and operational teams
Comfort using metrics and operating evidence to shape priorities
Strong judgment in fast-moving, ambiguous environments
Why this one is worth a look
Autonomous delivery only matters if the network can grow without each deployment becoming bespoke. This role is about the commercial and product operating system around the robots, which is where many robotics companies either compound or stall.

Zipline
South San Francisco robotics and autonomy company operating automated drone delivery systems.

Product
Program Manager, Major Deployments
Own scaled commercial drone deployments and feed field workflow lessons back into Skydio product and engineering teams.
What the role actually is
Skydio is hiring a program manager for major commercial deployments. The role owns rollout planning, operational handoff, and stabilization for customers moving from one-off drone use to recurring programs across multiple sites.
The posting spans piloted operations, dock-based remote operations, aviation compliance, training, maintenance, and feedback to Product and Engineering. It is a useful fit for the board because it sits where autonomous drone products meet real customer workflows.
What you would work on
Plan and execute major commercial drone deployments from pilot through scaled rollout
Build operating procedures, safety inputs, and support plans with customer teams
Manage deployment risks across hardware, software, operations, and compliance
Bring field lessons back to product and engineering for future platform improvements
What they are asking for
Program management experience with technical deployments, aviation, robotics, or complex field operations
Ability to coordinate customers, operators, safety leads, and internal technical teams
Comfort writing new playbooks for programs that do not yet have a standard pattern
Judgment around remote operations, docked drones, and operational readiness
Why this one is worth a look
The best robotics product lessons often come after launch, when customers try to run the system every day. This role is interesting because it turns those deployment realities into the feedback loop that determines whether autonomous drones become an operational product or remain pilots.

title: R&D Product Manager — Boston Dynamics — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
text:
R&D Product Manager — Boston Dynamics — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
Product
R&D Product Manager
Shape product discovery and end-to-end data-capture experiences for Boston Dynamics robotics and embodied AI work.
What the role actually is
Boston Dynamics is hiring an R&D product manager in Waltham for work around data capture, digital twins, and embodied AI workflows. The role sits between customers, designers, engineers, and robotics teams to turn field needs into product direction.
This is a product role for the messy middle between advanced robotics research and usable customer workflows.
What you would work on
Talk with customers on-site and remotely to understand how they use Boston Dynamics products
Scope proof-of-concept and pilot engagements that test product value in real settings
Prioritize and launch platform features with infrastructure, firmware, and software teams
Work with designers and engineers on software applications that connect internal and external workflows
Bring customer feedback back into the roadmap after launch
What they are asking for
Product management or founder experience with complex technical products
Experience with digital twins, laser scanning, virtual reality, or game-design-adjacent spatial products
Ability to turn customer requests into scoped product problems for engineering teams
Familiarity with robotics, IoT, or similarly physical technical systems
Comfort with occasional customer-site travel for testing, interviews, and observation
Why this one is worth a look
The interesting part is the digital-twin angle. Boston Dynamics already has robots that can collect data in the world; this role is about making the capture, interpretation, and customer workflow around that data coherent enough to become a product.

Boston Dynamics
Massachusetts robotics company behind Spot, Stretch, and Atlas, with work spanning mobile manipulation and humanoids.

title: Reinforcement Learning Engineer — Apptronik — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
text:
Reinforcement Learning Engineer — Apptronik — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
User Research
Reinforcement Learning Engineer
Build reinforcement learning policies for Apollo humanoid locomotion and manipulation.
What the role actually is
Apptronik is hiring a reinforcement learning engineer for its Apollo humanoid platform in Austin. The role is about making learned policies work for whole-body loco-manipulation on physical hardware.
The listing emphasizes the full loop from simulation prototypes to robot deployment, which makes this a real robot-learning role rather than a generic ML infrastructure position.
What you would work on
Implement reinforcement learning algorithms for locomotion and manipulation
Move policies from simulation into tests on physical humanoid hardware
Improve training pipelines for faster iteration and better transfer
Work with hardware, controls, and software teams on robot behavior
What they are asking for
Experience implementing reinforcement learning or robot-learning systems
Comfort with simulation-to-real transfer and physical robot constraints
Strong software engineering habits around experimentation and code review
Ability to collaborate across controls, hardware, and autonomy teams
Why this one is worth a look
Humanoid job postings can be vague, but this one names the behavior problem directly: dynamic locomotion and manipulation on hardware. That makes it a useful signal for candidates who want the hard part of humanoids, not just platform support.

text:
Research Engineer - AI/RL Infrastructure — Applied Intuition — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
User Research
Research Engineer - AI/RL Infrastructure
Build large-scale AI and reinforcement-learning infrastructure for Applied Intuition's physical AI research group.
What the role actually is
Applied Intuition is hiring a research engineer to build the AI and reinforcement-learning infrastructure behind its physical AI research. The role supports researchers working on autonomous driving and robotic generalist systems.
The focus is not just model training in isolation. The listing emphasizes large-scale ML systems that help researchers develop, accelerate, and evaluate methods for autonomous and robotic systems.
What you would work on
Design and operate infrastructure for AI, RL, and physical AI experiments
Work closely with researchers to make training and evaluation faster
Support research on autonomous driving, robotic generalists, and embodied systems
Improve reliability and scale for experiments that need to feed deployed programs
What they are asking for
Strong engineering experience with large-scale ML, reinforcement learning, or research infrastructure
Ability to partner closely with researchers on changing experimental needs
Practical judgment about compute, data, evaluation, and deployment constraints
Willingness to work onsite from Applied's Sunnyvale office
Why this one is worth a look
Infrastructure roles can be especially valuable in physical AI because research velocity depends on whether experiments are easy to run and trust. This one is close to Applied's autonomy and robotics research agenda, not a generic platform seat.

Research Engineer - New Grad (2027)
