Research Engineer - Reinforcement Learning, Self-Driving
Build reinforcement-learning systems for self-driving research inside Applied Intuition's physical AI research group.
What the role actually is
Applied Intuition is hiring research engineers for its AI research group. This opening focuses on reinforcement learning for self-driving systems, with the broader team working across end-to-end autonomy and robotic generalist research.
The role is research engineering rather than product design, but it fits the board's autonomy-research lane because evaluation, simulation, and behavior quality are central to whether autonomy becomes usable in the world.
What you would work on
Implement reinforcement-learning methods for autonomous driving research
Build experiments and tooling that help compare behavior policies
Work with researchers on physical AI systems spanning simulation and real-world autonomy
Translate research ideas into reliable code and repeatable evaluation loops
What they are asking for
Strong engineering background in ML, reinforcement learning, robotics, or autonomy
Ability to implement research methods and debug complex model behavior
Experience with experimentation, evaluation, and production-aware research workflows
Interest in self-driving systems and physical AI infrastructure
Why this one is worth a look
The interesting piece here is the infrastructure context. Reinforcement learning for autonomy only matters if teams can measure, compare, and trust behavior changes; Applied's business gives that research a direct path into autonomy tooling.

Research Engineer - Robotic Hardware, Simulation and Data — Applied Intuition — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
User Research
Research Engineer - Robotic Hardware, Simulation and Data
Build the hardware, simulation, and data loops behind Applied Intuition's physical AI research systems.
What the role actually is
Applied Intuition is looking for a research engineer focused on robotic hardware, simulation, and data for its physical AI research group. The work supports research on autonomous driving and robotic generalists, with an emphasis on turning experimental systems into practical development loops.
This is a research engineering role where the robot-facing stack matters: hardware behavior, simulated coverage, data quality, and evaluation all have to line up.
What you would work on
Build research infrastructure around robotic hardware, simulation, and data collection
Support experiments for embodied autonomy and robotic generalist systems
Help researchers evaluate methods on systems that reflect real deployment constraints
Improve the loop between simulated experiments, fleet data, and robot behavior
What they are asking for
Research engineering experience in robotics, autonomy, machine learning, simulation, or related systems
Ability to work across hardware-adjacent constraints, data pipelines, and model evaluation
Strong implementation skills for experiments that need to run reliably
Comfort collaborating with a research group in an in-office Sunnyvale environment
Why this one is worth a look
This is a good fit for someone who likes the practical side of robotics research. Applied is explicit that the research group is working across autonomous vehicles, industrial machines, humanoids, and dexterous hands, so the infrastructure work has a broad physical AI surface area.

User Research
Research Intern - Reinforcement Learning, Robotics
Work with Applied Intuition's research group on reinforcement learning for robotic generalist systems.
What the role actually is
Applied Intuition is looking for research interns focused on reinforcement learning for robotics. The posting places the work in a research group building technology for physical AI, including robotic generalists, humanoids, and dexterous hands.
The role is best suited to someone who wants an internship close to model research, simulation, and embodied autonomy rather than a conventional software internship.
What you would work on
Run reinforcement learning experiments for robotic and embodied AI systems
Use simulation and fleet-scale infrastructure to evaluate learned behavior
Collaborate with researchers working across autonomy and robotics
Contribute research code that can inform practical physical AI systems
What they are asking for
Active research interest in reinforcement learning, robotics, or embodied AI
Ability to implement and evaluate learning-based methods
Comfort moving between papers, experiments, and working systems
Interest in physical robot behavior, not just abstract model training
Why this one is worth a look
Internships in robot learning are often either academic lab roles or narrow platform internships. This one is notable because Applied is building infrastructure that can touch self-driving, humanoids, dexterous manipulation, and industrial autonomy under one research umbrella.

Help build or evaluate research prototypes in a production-adjacent environment

Graduate-level or equivalent research exposure in ML, robotics, embodied AI, or foundation models

Comfort working from the Sunnyvale office during the internship

Research Scientist - 3D Vision and Generation, Self-Driving

Turn research findings into methods that can influence customer-facing systems

Comfort working with real-world autonomous-system constraints

Research Scientist - Humanoid Robotics
Research humanoid robotics methods for Applied Intuition's physical AI group.
What the role actually is
Applied Intuition is hiring a research scientist focused on humanoid robotics. The work is tied to the company's AI research group and its push into generalist physical AI systems.
This is a research-heavy role, but it belongs on the board because humanoid systems are ultimately judged by what they can do around people, tools, tasks, and messy environments.
What you would work on
Research learning and control methods for humanoid robot behavior
Build experiments that connect simulation, data, and embodied performance
Collaborate with researchers and engineers on next-generation physical AI systems
Help turn research insight into reusable infrastructure for robotics teams
What they are asking for
Research depth in robotics, machine learning, humanoids, or embodied AI
Ability to design experiments and evaluate robot behavior rigorously
Strong publication, implementation, or applied research record
Comfort working in a fast-moving industrial research environment
Why this one is worth a look
Humanoid robotics is crowded with demos, but fewer companies are building the infrastructure layer around it. Applied's role is interesting because it links humanoid research to broader autonomy tooling and simulation products.

title: Research Scientist, Mobile Manipulation Robotics — Amazon Robotics — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
text:
Research Scientist, Mobile Manipulation Robotics — Amazon Robotics — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
User Research
Research Scientist, Mobile Manipulation Robotics
Advance mobile-manipulation research for Amazon Robotics systems operating in dynamic fulfillment environments.
What the role actually is
Amazon Robotics is hiring a research scientist in North Reading for mobile manipulation. The role focuses on learning-based approaches that help robots navigate and manipulate objects in dynamic fulfillment environments.
This is applied robotics research with an explicit path from experiments to production systems.
What you would work on
Formulate research problems in robot learning and mobile manipulation
Design model architectures, experiments, benchmarks, and ablation studies
Define data requirements and reusable pipelines for robotics research
Build research code and evaluation tooling for broader robotics integration
What they are asking for
PhD or equivalent research depth in a quantitative or robotics-adjacent field
Experience designing experiments and statistically validating results
Strong Python and deep-learning framework experience
Ability to explain complex technical work to both technical and non-technical audiences
Why this one is worth a look
Amazon Robotics is one of the few places where mobile manipulation research can meet enormous operational scale. The tradeoff is that the research agenda is tightly coupled to fulfillment problems, so the best fit is someone who wants production constraints close to the science.

Amazon Robotics

title: Research Scientist - Reinforcement Learning, Robotics — Applied Intuition — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
text:
Research Scientist - Reinforcement Learning, Robotics — Applied Intuition — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
User Research
Research Scientist - Reinforcement Learning, Robotics
Research reinforcement-learning methods for robotics and embodied AI at Applied Intuition.
What the role actually is
Applied Intuition is hiring a research scientist focused on reinforcement learning for robotics. The role is part of its AI research group, which is working on physical AI for autonomous driving and robotic generalist systems.
This is not a UX role, but it belongs on the research side of the board because reinforcement learning affects the behavior layer people ultimately have to understand, trust, and work around.
What you would work on
Develop reinforcement-learning methods for robotic systems
Design experiments that measure embodied behavior and generalization
Collaborate with research engineers on simulation, data, and evaluation workflows
Help turn robotics research into reusable physical AI infrastructure
What they are asking for
Research background in reinforcement learning, robotics, or embodied AI
Ability to frame, run, and evaluate technical research programs
Strong publication, implementation, or applied research record
Comfort working closely with engineering teams in an in-office environment
Why this one is worth a look
Robotics needs learning methods that hold up outside narrow demos. This role is a signal that Applied is investing in the policy-learning layer behind robotic generalists, while staying close to the infrastructure used by autonomy teams.

Applied Intuition

title: Research Scientist, VLA Models - Atlas — Boston Dynamics — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
text:
Research Scientist, VLA Models - Atlas — Boston Dynamics — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
User Research
Research Scientist, VLA Models - Atlas
Train and deploy vision-language-action behavior models for dexterous manipulation on Atlas.
What the role actually is
Boston Dynamics is hiring a research scientist for VLA models on Atlas. The role focuses on large behavior models that use vision, language, task context, and robot state to produce grounded actions for humanoid manipulation.
This is robot-learning research with a direct hardware loop, not a purely offline modeling job.
What you would work on
Architect and train VLA and large behavior models for mobile manipulation
Build imitation learning pipelines from demonstrations, teleoperation, and simulation data
Develop policies that generalize across manipulation tasks and environments
Create hierarchical behavior systems for longer-horizon Atlas tasks
Integrate learned components into the Atlas autonomy stack and test them on hardware
What they are asking for
Graduate-level machine learning, robotics, computer science, or related research background
Experience training and deploying learned policies for robots or simulated characters
Depth in large behavior models, sequence modeling, or multimodal learning
Practical experience with PyTorch, JAX, and large-scale training workflows
Comfort debugging learned policies on physical robotic systems
Why this one is worth a look
Atlas roles are a useful signal for where humanoid robotics is moving: away from demos as isolated behaviors and toward reusable learned skills. The caveat is that this is a deep technical research seat, but its output will shape how people eventually interact with a general-purpose humanoid.

Boston Dynamics
Massachusetts robotics company behind Spot, Stretch, and Atlas, with work spanning mobile manipulation and humanoids.

text:
Research Scientist - World-Action Foundation Model, Robotics — Applied Intuition — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
User Research
Research Scientist - World-Action Foundation Model, Robotics
Research world-action foundation models for robotic generalist systems inside Applied Intuition's physical AI group.
What the role actually is
Applied Intuition is hiring research scientists for its AI research group, with this posting focused on world-action foundation models for robotics. The team frames the work around next-generation physical AI, especially end-to-end autonomous driving and robotic generalists.
This is an in-office Sunnyvale research role. It is relevant to the board because the work is about how embodied systems represent the world, choose actions, and generalize across tasks.
What you would work on
Research world-action model approaches for robots and autonomous systems
Build experiments that connect model behavior to physical AI performance
Work with a research group spanning robotics, autonomy, simulation, and data
Turn research results into infrastructure that can support real robotic systems
What they are asking for
Research strength in machine learning, robotics, embodied AI, or foundation models
Ability to design and evaluate experiments for action-generating systems
Publication, implementation, or applied research evidence in relevant areas
Comfort working in a highly technical in-office research environment
Why this one is worth a look
World models are becoming a central bet in robot learning. Applied's angle is worth tracking because it is trying to connect that research to infrastructure for moving machines, not only to a lab demo or a single robot form factor.

Applied Intuition

text:
Robot Learning Engineer - Manipulation — Applied Intuition — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
User Research
Robot Learning Engineer - Manipulation
Train and deploy manipulation policies for Applied Intuition's Dana robot-learning platform.
What the role actually is
Applied Intuition is hiring a robot learning engineer for manipulation work on Dana, its physical AI platform. The role covers the full learning loop: task definition, demonstration collection, data curation, training, evaluation, and deployment on physical robots.
The listing is explicit that success is measured on real robots in customer-relevant industrial tasks, not just offline benchmarks. That makes it a practical robot-learning role with a direct path to deployed autonomy.
What you would work on
Train and fine-tune manipulation policies for industrial robot tasks
Build repeatable recipes for pick-and-place, bimanual handling, and contact-rich assembly
Validate policy behavior on physical robots, including observation processing and control timing
Turn failures and human interventions into better data, models, and evaluation loops
Package learned behaviors so new tasks and robot platforms can start from prior work
What they are asking for
Experience training or fine-tuning learned manipulation policies
Practical depth in imitation learning and modern policy families such as VLA models, diffusion policies, or action-chunking transformers
Strong Python and PyTorch skills for training, evaluation, and deployment code
Working knowledge of robot kinematics, coordinate frames, camera calibration, and low-level control interfaces
Comfort diagnosing failures through controlled experiments across data, sensing, model, and execution
Why this one is worth a look
Manipulation is where robot learning has to prove it can survive messy, physical work. This role is interesting because it sits inside a platform company trying to make learned industrial robot behavior repeatable across tasks, not just impressive in one demo.

Applied Intuition
Silicon Valley physical AI company building autonomy, simulation, and operating-system software for vehicles, drones, defense systems, and industrial machines.

title: Robotics Algorithms Engineer, Manipulation & Control — Path Robotics — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
text:
Robotics Algorithms Engineer, Manipulation & Control — Path Robotics — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
User Research
Robotics Algorithms Engineer, Manipulation & Control
Own real-time control and state-estimation algorithms for Path's high-accuracy robotic manipulation systems.
What the role actually is
Path Robotics is hiring a manipulation and control algorithms engineer in Columbus. The role owns the closed loop from sensing to motion for industrial robot arms and end effectors, including state estimation, predictive control, and trajectory correction on real hardware.
This is a technical research-engineering role, but it fits the board because the work is directly about robot manipulation behavior: how a production robot senses, moves, handles uncertainty, and fails safely.
What you would work on
Build real-time control and state-estimation systems for sensor-guided manipulation
Design feedback and predictive control loops that correct end-effector motion under uncertainty
Set technical direction for learning-based and whole-body control work
Reason about how perception errors affect motion accuracy
Ship hard-real-time robotics software that runs reliably on physical systems
What they are asking for
Deep experience with real-time control, state estimation, and robotic manipulation
Familiarity with model-predictive control, Kalman or particle filters, observability, or moving-horizon estimation
Hands-on background with arm kinematics, dynamics, trajectory generation, and calibration
Experience with sensor-guided motion, visual servoing, or closed perception-to-control loops
Strong production C++, ROS or ROS 2, and real-time systems discipline
Why this one is worth a look
Industrial manipulation is where elegant robotics ideas meet unforgiving tolerances. Path's role is interesting because it is not just model work; it asks someone to make sensing, control, calibration, and real hardware behavior line up inside a production welding system.

Path Robotics
Columbus robotics company building AI-driven robotic welding systems for industrial production environments.

text:
Senior 3D Generalist, Product Visualization — Skydio — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
Marketing
Senior 3D Generalist, Product Visualization
Create photorealistic 3D product imagery, animations, and interactive assets for Skydio launches and brand work.
What the role actually is
Skydio is hiring a senior 3D generalist for a full-time, three-month contract on its Brand Creative team. The role turns product CAD into polished imagery, animations, illustrations, and interactive 3D assets for launches, keynote work, and web experiences.
This is not product design in the UX sense, but it is highly product-specific creative work for autonomous drones and belongs in the board's marketing and design-adjacent lane.
What you would work on
Build photorealistic drone product renderings, illustrations, and animations
Prepare CAD-derived geometry for production visualization in Blender
Create assets for product launches, keynotes, web experiences, manuals, decks, and campaigns
Preserve product accuracy while lighting, materializing, animating, and compositing scenes
Optimize real-time or interactive 3D assets when a project calls for them
What they are asking for
Portfolio or reel showing hard-surface product rendering and product animation
Strong lighting, material-development, and CAD-derived visualization skills
Ability to clean geometry, organize scenes, create UVs, and preserve product proportions
Experience with Blender and production-ready product visualization workflows
U.S. work authorization for a remote or San Mateo hybrid contract
Why this one is worth a look
Robotics products are physical, expensive, and often hard to photograph in every useful state. This role is relevant because it makes the product legible before, during, and after launch by translating engineering models into credible public-facing visuals.

This is not product design in the UX sense, but it is highly product-specific creative work for autonomous drones and belongs in the board's marketing and design-adjacent lane.
What you would work on
Build photorealistic drone product renderings, illustrations, and animations
Prepare CAD-derived geometry for production visualization in Blender
Create assets for product launches, keynotes, web experiences, manuals, decks, and campaigns
Preserve product accuracy while lighting, materializing, animating, and compositing scenes
Optimize real-time or interactive 3D assets when a project calls for them
What they are asking for
Portfolio or reel showing hard-surface product rendering and product animation
Strong lighting, material-development, and CAD-derived visualization skills
Ability to clean geometry, organize scenes, create UVs, and preserve product proportions
Experience with Blender and production-ready product visualization workflows
U.S. work authorization for a remote or San Mateo hybrid contract
Why this one is worth a look
Robotics products are physical, expensive, and often hard to photograph in every useful state. This role is relevant because it makes the product legible before, during, and after launch by translating engineering models into credible public-facing visuals.

title: Senior AI Software Engineer, Reinforcement Learning — Agility — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
text:
Senior AI Software Engineer, Reinforcement Learning — Agility — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
User Research
Senior AI Software Engineer, Reinforcement Learning
Develop and deploy reinforcement-learning policies for Digit locomotion, manipulation, and whole-body control.
What the role actually is
This is a robot-learning role on Agility's AI Controls team. The person would train, evaluate, and ship reinforcement-learning policies that let Digit move safely and reliably in production environments.
What you would work on
Train RL policies for locomotion, manipulation, whole-body control, and dynamic interaction.
Integrate perception into policies for obstacle-aware motion and perceptive manipulation.
Build scalable training pipelines, simulation tasks, and evaluation infrastructure.
Work with on-robot software and deployment teams to get learned policies onto deployed humanoids.
What they are asking for
Experience developing and deploying RL policies for robotics applications.
Strong Python and deep-learning framework skills.
Familiarity with reward design, hyperparameter tuning, and exploration strategies for control tasks.
Comfort turning simulation and evaluation work into production robot behavior.
Why this one is worth a look
Agility is one of the few humanoid companies with robots already running in customer facilities. The role is engineering-heavy, but it is directly about learned behavior for robots operating around people, which makes it relevant for anyone tracking the practical edge of robot learning.

Senior Applied Scientist, Navigation

What the role actually is
Amazon Robotics is hiring a senior applied scientist focused on robot navigation. The role combines learning-based planning, foundation models for embodied agents, and control-theoretic methods such as model-predictive trajectory planning.
The work is aimed at navigation systems that can move safely and fluidly through changing operational environments rather than only passing static benchmarks.
What you would work on
Research navigation systems that combine data-driven learning with control guarantees
Develop planning and perception methods for dynamic robotics environments
Connect academic advances in embodied AI with production-grade deployment needs

Communication skills for cross-functional work with scientists, engineers, and product managers
Why this one is worth a look
Navigation is one of the places where autonomy becomes visible to nearby humans. A system can be technically capable and still feel unsafe or illegible if it moves poorly, so this is a research role with direct consequences for human-facing robot behavior.

title: Senior Applied Scientist, Robot Capability Evaluation, Fauna — Fauna Robotics — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
text:
Senior Applied Scientist, Robot Capability Evaluation, Fauna — Fauna Robotics — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
User Research
Senior Applied Scientist, Robot Capability Evaluation, Fauna
Build evaluation frameworks and data protocols for measuring Fauna's robot capabilities.
What the role actually is
Fauna is hiring a senior applied scientist to define how robot capabilities are measured, stress-tested, and improved. The posting ties evaluation to data collection protocols, teleoperation workflows, task definitions, and model development.
This is a research infrastructure role, but it is close to product reality because the metrics determine which robot behaviors are considered ready for real homes.
What you would work on
Design evaluation frameworks for robot tasks, edge cases, and real-world scenarios
Define benchmarks, task structures, and success criteria for embodied policies
Shape data collection protocols that support model improvement
Iterate on teleoperation and operator-facing workflows for reliable evaluation
What they are asking for
Applied science experience in robotics, machine learning, evaluation, or human-in-the-loop systems
Ability to turn ambiguous capability goals into measurable tests
Comfort with both experimental design and systems constraints
Experience connecting evaluation data to model or policy development
Why this one is worth a look
Evaluation is becoming one of the core bottlenecks in embodied AI. This role is worth tracking because whoever owns the benchmark effectively shapes what the robot is allowed to become.

Fauna Robotics
Amazon-owned robotics team building safe, expressive robots for everyday human spaces.

Senior Curriculum Developer, sUAS Operations
Architect training curricula for Skydio pilots and technicians working with autonomous drone systems.
What the role actually is
Skydio is hiring a senior curriculum developer for sUAS operations. The role owns the instructional backbone of training programs: task analysis, learning objectives, assessments, certification paths, and sequencing across multiple delivery formats.

What you would work on
Define curriculum architecture for pilots, technicians, and internal teams

What they are asking for
Curriculum development experience for technical or operational audiences
Ability to translate complex systems into performance-based learning paths
Comfort designing assessments, course maps, and certification structures
Interest in autonomous drone operations and real-world user readiness
Why this one is worth a look
As robotics products mature, training becomes part of the product surface. Skydio's curriculum role is a good example: the work shapes how real operators become competent with autonomous systems, not just how docs get written.

text:
Senior Electrical Engineer - HRI (Visuals) — Apptronik — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
Design and UX
Senior Electrical Engineer - HRI (Visuals)
Own the display and lighting electronics that make Apptronik's Apollo humanoid visually legible to nearby people.
What the role actually is
Apptronik is hiring a senior electrical engineer for the visual side of Apollo's human-robot interface. The work centers on display and LED lighting electronics, from requirements and architecture through prototypes, validation, production release, and support.
This is an engineering role, but it belongs on the board because the posting explicitly ties the hardware to HRI and asks the person to translate industrial design and UX intent into measurable visual-system requirements.
What you would work on
Define electronics requirements for Apollo's visual HRI subsystem
Design, bring up, and test display and LED lighting PCBAs
Translate industrial design and UX intent into electrical and optical requirements
Validate luminance, color, uniformity, viewing angle, thermal behavior, and reliability
Own visual HRI hardware from concept through production release and support
Coordinate with suppliers, contract manufacturers, and external design partners
What they are asking for
Senior-level experience designing display or LED lighting electronics
Strong mixed-signal PCB design skills and comfort with modern PCB tools
Experience with LED drivers, RGB LED arrays, brightness control, color control, and thermal management
Experience integrating display modules and related power, backlight, and interface electronics
Ability to design and execute electrical and optical validation tests
Interest in working with industrial design, mechanical design, and user-facing operator interfaces
Why this one is worth a look
Many HRI jobs are software or research posts; this one is about the physical signals a humanoid gives to people standing near it. For someone who cares about robot legibility, the role is interesting because the display and lighting hardware will constrain what Apollo can communicate before any app or dashboard is involved.

title: Senior Industrial Designer — Amazon Robotics — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
text:
Senior Industrial Designer — Amazon Robotics — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
Design and UX
Senior Industrial Designer
Shape industrial design and user experience for robotic systems, workstations, and physical automation touchpoints.
What the role actually is
Amazon Robotics is hiring a senior industrial designer to translate robotic system requirements into physical and experiential design decisions. The role spans concepts, implementation, detailed design documentation, vendor collaboration, and design standards for industrial automation.
This is a product design role in the literal physical sense: the work affects how people encounter robotic systems, workstations, components, motion, scale, and safety cues inside operational environments.
What you would work on
Lead industrial design projects from concept through implementation
Design physical interfaces, workstations, and system touchpoints for robotic automation
Build documentation, specifications, and presentations for stakeholder review
Use tools such as CAD, visualization, VR, AR, or generative AI to evaluate form and interaction
What they are asking for
Senior industrial design experience for technical products or industrial systems
Working knowledge of CAD and advanced assembly design practices
Experience leading design work across concepting, prototyping, implementation, and stakeholder review
Portfolio evidence of systems thinking, UX-aware form development, and robotics or automation context
Why this one is worth a look
Industrial design often gets flattened into hardware aesthetics, but robotics makes it operational. This role is about making physical automation more legible, usable, and safe at Amazon's scale, where a design choice becomes part of the work environment.
About
Amazon Robotics
Amazon's robotics organization designs the automation systems, service workflows, and human-facing tools used across fulfillment operations.

title: Senior Industrial Designer, Fauna — Fauna Robotics — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
text:
Senior Industrial Designer, Fauna — Fauna Robotics — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
Design and UX
Senior Industrial Designer, Fauna
Lead production surfacing and finish decisions for Fauna's robot exterior hardware.
What the role actually is
Fauna is hiring a senior industrial designer to refine robot exterior parts from approved design intent into production-ready surfaces. The job sits close to mechanical design, tooling, CMF, and cosmetic finish decisions.
The work is about making the robot's visible hardware feel deliberate while still respecting draft, wall thickness, assembly, manufacturing constraints, and vendor realities.
What you would work on
Lead Class A surface development for exterior robot components
Turn sketches or concept geometry into production-intent 3D models
Resolve DFM issues with design engineering and manufacturing partners
Define cosmetic finish and CMF details that hold up at scale
What they are asking for
Senior experience in industrial design, design innovation, or product R&D
CAD fluency and comfort managing engineering-heavy design projects
Ability to make tradeoffs across aesthetics, tooling, manufacturing, and cost
Experience collaborating with mechanical, hardware, and vendor teams
Why this one is worth a look
Fauna's robot is meant for everyday human spaces, so industrial design is not just styling. The exterior has to communicate safety, personality, durability, and intent before a user reads a screen or hears a prompt.

Fauna Robotics
Amazon-owned robotics team building safe, expressive robots for everyday human spaces.

text:
Senior Learning Experience Developer — Skydio — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
User Research
Senior Learning Experience Developer
Design learning experiences that help pilots and technicians operate Skydio autonomous drones safely.
What the role actually is
Skydio is hiring a senior learning experience developer for its training team. The role turns complex autonomous drone workflows into classroom, self-paced, simulation, and immersive learning experiences.
This is not a conventional UX research job, but it is squarely about the human side of robotics: how operators learn, trust, and safely use autonomous systems in the field.
What you would work on
Design learner-centered training experiences for pilots and technicians
Translate drone systems and operational procedures into usable instruction
Build media, simulation, and immersive training materials
Partner with instructors, curriculum developers, product teams, and subject experts
What they are asking for
Learning experience design or instructional media experience
Ability to make complex technical systems understandable to operators
Comfort working across classroom, digital, simulation, and immersive formats
Interest in improving field performance for autonomous drone users
Why this one is worth a look
Robotics adoption often fails at the training layer. Skydio's role is interesting because it treats operator readiness as a product problem, especially as drone workflows become more autonomous and simulation-driven.

title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer - 3D Reconstruction — Applied Intuition — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
text:
Senior Machine Learning Engineer - 3D Reconstruction — Applied Intuition — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
User Research
Senior Machine Learning Engineer - 3D Reconstruction
Advance 3D reconstruction methods that turn fleet data into high-fidelity simulation for autonomy teams.
What the role actually is
Applied Intuition is hiring a senior ML engineer to improve the reconstruction technology behind Neural Simulation. The team turns real driving data into photorealistic environments that customers use to train, test, and validate autonomy systems.
The posting calls out 3D Gaussian Splatting, NeRFs, dynamic actor reconstruction, scene editing, novel-view synthesis, and multi-sensor rendering. It is a production research role for simulation fidelity and scale.
What you would work on
Improve learning-based reconstruction methods for large, dynamic driving scenes
Productionize techniques such as Gaussian splatting, NeRFs, and feed-forward reconstruction
Support camera and LiDAR rendering for autonomy simulation workflows
Build evaluation metrics for reconstruction fidelity and sim-to-real gap
Collaborate with autonomy, infrastructure, research, and product teams on end-to-end simulation quality
What they are asking for
Strong background in 3D computer vision, graphics, machine learning, or neural rendering
Experience moving research methods into production systems
Ability to reason about reconstruction quality, throughput, and customer-facing simulation needs
Interest in physical AI, autonomy validation, and large-scale fleet-data pipelines
Why this one is worth a look
The role is a good signal of where autonomy tooling is moving: better simulation is not just prettier scenes, but a way to close validation gaps using real-world fleet data. The caveat is that this is deeply technical product infrastructure rather than a pure robotics lab role.

Applied Intuition

title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer - Generative Models — Applied Intuition — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
text:
Senior Machine Learning Engineer - Generative Models — Applied Intuition — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
User Research
Senior Machine Learning Engineer - Generative Models
Build generative simulation models that create controllable driving-scene data for autonomy training and validation.
What the role actually is
Applied Intuition is hiring a senior ML engineer for the generative-modeling side of its Neural Simulation product. The work focuses on diffusion and video generation models that turn real-world driving data into controllable, photorealistic simulation scenarios.
The role sits at the research-to-product boundary: improving realism, temporal consistency, controllability, and evaluation workflows so autonomy teams can train and validate systems against harder simulated conditions.
What you would work on
Develop diffusion and video-generation models for driving-scene simulation
Generate sensor data conditioned on scene layout, camera pose, actors, and trajectories
Augment real-world logs with new scenarios, actors, weather, and lighting conditions
Define metrics and benchmarks for realism, temporal consistency, controllability, and sim-to-real gap
Work with autonomy, infrastructure, research, and customer-facing teams to productionize new methods
What they are asking for
Strong ML experience in generative modeling, computer vision, or related areas
Ability to bring recent research into production systems
Experience with large-model training or inference workflows
Interest in autonomy simulation and evaluation for physical AI systems
Why this one is worth a look
Simulation quality is becoming a core constraint for autonomy teams. This role is interesting because it applies fast-moving generative-model research to concrete validation problems for vehicles and other moving machines.

Applied Intuition

text:

User Research
Senior Machine Learning Engineer, Tech Lead, Robot Learning, Loco-Manipulation
Lead Path's robot-learning work on whole-body loco-manipulation for industrial robots.
What the role actually is
Path Robotics is hiring a senior machine learning engineer and tech lead for its loco-manipulation robot-learning work. The person will write code, set technical direction, make architectural calls, mentor engineers, and shape the team's working model.
The role can be based in Columbus or remote, and it sits at the beginning of a new research stack for precision heavy-manufacturing tasks.
What you would work on
Set technical direction for ML systems that drive whole-body loco-manipulation
Build architecture for visual reasoning, learned action policies, and RL fine-tuning
Mentor engineers while staying hands-on in implementation
Evaluate models against real industrial robot behavior and customer data
What they are asking for
Senior ML engineering experience in robotics, manipulation, or embodied AI
Ability to lead technical architecture while still writing production-quality code
Experience with learned policies, reinforcement learning, or robot-control systems
Judgment about turning research ideas into reliable industrial capability
Why this one is worth a look
Founding tech-lead roles can be high-leverage when the team is pointed at a real bottleneck. Here the bottleneck is getting learned robot behavior to perform precision physical work, not just benchmark well.

User Research
Senior Manager, Learning from Demonstration
Lead research programs that turn learning-from-demonstration work into usable capabilities for Agility's humanoid robots.
What the role actually is
Agility is hiring a senior manager to lead learning-from-demonstration research for its humanoid platform. The role sits between AI/ML research and product-roadmap risk, with a mandate to move promising ideas toward proof-of-concept robot deployments.
The posting names real-time planning, whole-body control, and demonstration learning as core areas. This is a research leadership role, but the useful signal is that Agility wants research tied to capabilities it may need to ship in the next one to two years.
What you would work on
Lead innovation projects from research framing through robot proof of concept
Manage a team of researchers and engineers working on humanoid robot capabilities
Drive learning-from-demonstration, planning, and control work against product-roadmap risks
Build a research culture around rigorous experiments, fast iteration, and delivery quality
What they are asking for
Leadership experience in robotics, AI, ML, or adjacent applied research
Depth in robot learning, planning, controls, or humanoid robotics
Ability to connect research bets to functional robot capabilities
Comfort managing technical teams in a remote U.S. role
Why this one is worth a look
Learning from demonstration is one of the clearer bridges between today's humanoid demos and robots that can absorb new tasks in real settings. Agility's role is interesting because it treats that bridge as both a research agenda and a product-risk function.

title: Senior ML Engineer, Manipulation — Chef Robotics — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
text:
Senior ML Engineer, Manipulation — Chef Robotics — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
User Research
Senior ML Engineer, Manipulation
Build and evaluate manipulation policies for Chef Robotics' food-assembly automation systems.
What the role actually is
Chef Robotics is hiring a senior ML engineer focused on manipulation in San Francisco. The role designs and trains policies for robotic food handling, including imitation learning, reinforcement learning, diffusion policies, and transformer-based action models.
The listing is technical, but it is directly relevant to robot learning: the work turns production food-handling data, teleoperation, and evaluation pipelines into manipulation behavior that can run on real robots.
What you would work on
Design and train learned manipulation policies for variable food items and end effectors
Build data collection and training pipelines with teleoperation and kinesthetic teaching inputs
Evaluate policy architectures such as diffusion policies and action-model transformers
Adapt models for production robots handling deformable and inconsistent materials
What they are asking for
Robotics, machine learning, or computer science depth at senior engineering level
Experience with robot manipulation, visuomotor control, imitation learning, or reinforcement learning
Strong PyTorch and production-minded ML system implementation skills
Comfort testing learned policies against real-world robot constraints
Why this one is worth a look
Food manipulation is a hard physical AI problem because the objects are inconsistent, deformable, and messy. Chef's production deployments make this a useful signal for anyone watching robot learning move beyond lab tasks into commercial operations.

Senior Motion Designer
Create motion graphics and technical explainers for Zipline's products, operations, launches, and customer stories.
What the role actually is
Zipline is hiring a senior motion designer for its communications and brand work. The role turns product launches, technical concepts, operational footage, interfaces, maps, diagrams, and customer stories into finished motion assets.
This is a hands-on creative role for someone who can make autonomous logistics clear and credible without flattening the technical details.
What you would work on
Design and animate motion graphics for product launches, explainers, social video, events, web, and presentations
Translate briefs, scripts, brand systems, and technical information into storyboards, style frames, animatics, and final animation
Build visual explanations of Zipline products and operations using typography, maps, diagrams, data, interfaces, callouts, and 2D or 3D animation
Composite graphics into live-action footage, including screen replacements, tracked graphics, masks, cleanup, and shot-based effects
Collaborate with communications, brand, social, marketing, engineering, operators, video production, and editing partners
Maintain reusable templates, animation components, title systems, project files, and production documentation
What they are asking for
Professional motion design experience with a strong reel or portfolio
Expert After Effects ability, plus strong working proficiency in Illustrator, Photoshop, and Figma
3D animation experience in Cinema 4D, Blender, or a similar package
Strong typography, composition, color, hierarchy, timing, pacing, and animation fundamentals
Ability to explain complex products, systems, data, and technical concepts through motion
Experience with robotics, autonomy, aviation, logistics, hardware, infrastructure, healthcare, or another technical field is a plus
Why this one is worth a look
This is not a core robot-building job, but it belongs on the board because Zipline's U.S. expansion depends on making autonomous delivery understandable and acceptable to customers, communities, and partners. The role is a useful signal that product storytelling around robots is becoming more technical, more operational, and more central to deployment.

Zipline is hiring a senior motion designer for its communications and brand work. The role turns product launches, technical concepts, operational footage, interfaces, maps, diagrams, and customer stories into finished motion assets.
This is a hands-on creative role for someone who can make autonomous logistics clear and credible without flattening the technical details.
What you would work on
Design and animate motion graphics for product launches, explainers, social video, events, web, and presentations
Translate briefs, scripts, brand systems, and technical information into storyboards, style frames, animatics, and final animation
Build visual explanations of Zipline products and operations using typography, maps, diagrams, data, interfaces, callouts, and 2D or 3D animation
Composite graphics into live-action footage, including screen replacements, tracked graphics, masks, cleanup, and shot-based effects
Collaborate with communications, brand, social, marketing, engineering, operators, video production, and editing partners
Maintain reusable templates, animation components, title systems, project files, and production documentation
What they are asking for
Professional motion design experience with a strong reel or portfolio
Expert After Effects ability, plus strong working proficiency in Illustrator, Photoshop, and Figma
3D animation experience in Cinema 4D, Blender, or a similar package
Strong typography, composition, color, hierarchy, timing, pacing, and animation fundamentals
Ability to explain complex products, systems, data, and technical concepts through motion
Experience with robotics, autonomy, aviation, logistics, hardware, infrastructure, healthcare, or another technical field is a plus
Why this one is worth a look
This is not a core robot-building job, but it belongs on the board because Zipline's U.S. expansion depends on making autonomous delivery understandable and acceptable to customers, communities, and partners. The role is a useful signal that product storytelling around robots is becoming more technical, more operational, and more central to deployment.

title: Senior Product Designer — Gecko Robotics — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
text:
Senior Product Designer — Gecko Robotics — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
Design and UX
Senior Product Designer
Design manufacturing and defense workflows around robot-collected inspection data, asset health, and operational decisions.
What the role actually is
Gecko Robotics is hiring a senior product designer for manufacturing and defense work. The role sits around the data layer created by field robots: inspection evidence, asset condition, operational risk, and the interfaces that help industrial teams act on that information.
This is not a cute robot UI job. It is a serious systems-design role where the user may be an engineer, maintenance leader, plant operator, or defense customer trying to make decisions from hard-won inspection data.
What you would work on
Shape product workflows for manufacturing and defense customers using robot-collected infrastructure data
Turn complex inspection findings into usable interfaces for planning, triage, and decision-making
Work with product, engineering, and field teams to understand how robotic inspection data moves from site work into software
Build design patterns that can support high-consequence operational environments
What they are asking for
Senior product design experience in complex technical or enterprise products
Comfort designing around dense data, operational workflows, and multi-stakeholder decisions
Ability to collaborate closely with product managers, engineers, and customer-facing teams
Interest in industrial, manufacturing, defense, or infrastructure contexts
Why this one is worth a look
Gecko is a useful reminder that the robot is often only the first part of the product. The value comes when inspection data becomes something a plant, shipyard, or asset owner can trust enough to act on. For designers, that makes the role less about robot controls and more about making physical-world evidence legible inside an organization.

Gecko Robotics

What the role actually is
Nuro is hiring a senior product designer in Mountain View for its autonomous driving product work. The role is a fit for a designer who can turn complex autonomy, operations, and customer requirements into clear product experiences.

Senior Product Designer
Design HMI and ground-control station workflows for operators commanding Shield AI autonomous aircraft.
What the role actually is
Shield AI is hiring a senior product designer focused on human-machine interfaces for ground control station software. The role designs the displays, flows, and interaction patterns operators use to plan, command, and monitor autonomous aircraft.
This is a classic high-stakes robotics UX role. The designer has to make complex system state understandable under operational pressure, while working with pilots, systems engineers, software teams, and human factors experts.
What you would work on
Design HMI systems for UAV ground control station displays
Turn complex autonomy and aircraft requirements into operator-facing interfaces
Create user flows, wireframes, high-fidelity mockups, and Figma prototypes
Apply human factors principles around workload, usability, and situational awareness
What they are asking for
Product design or HMI experience for complex technical systems
Strong prototyping and visual design ability for mission-critical interfaces
Comfort collaborating with operators, pilots, engineers, and human factors specialists
Ability to reason about safety, workload, and clarity under time pressure
Why this one is worth a look
Ground control design is where autonomy still has to answer to human judgment. The role is valuable because it deals directly with how operators understand, trust, and intervene in robotic systems when the cost of confusion is high.

Senior Product Manager, Dock Hardware Platform

Experience defining and delivering hardware products with connected software experiences.

Experience with commercial, public safety, or defense hardware markets, or a clear interest in them.

Docked drones are where autonomy becomes infrastructure instead of a single device sale. This role sits at that intersection: fleet reliability, physical deployment, user workflows, and the product decisions that make autonomous drone operations repeatable.

text:
Senior Product Manager, Fleet and Internal Tools — Skydio — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
Product
Senior Product Manager, Fleet and Internal Tools
Shape Skydio's fleet management and internal tooling for drone operations, service, repair, and support workflows.
What the role actually is
Skydio is hiring a senior product manager for Fleet Management and Internal Tools on the Skydio Cloud platform. The role spans customer-facing fleet software and the internal systems that support drone operations, service, repair, troubleshooting, and customer experience.
The job is about making autonomous drone fleets easier to operate at scale. That means turning telemetry, support data, fragmented service workflows, and field feedback into a coherent product roadmap.
What you would work on
Own fleet management and internal tooling roadmaps across device health, inventory, administration, support, service, and repair
Define dock service workflows from issue detection and remote diagnosis through dispatch, parts, verification, and closure
Prototype and validate workflows that simplify operational complexity for customers
Coordinate product work across cloud, UX, hardware, firmware, operations, support, and go-to-market teams
What they are asking for
Product experience shipping software for fleet, logistics, mobility, or similarly complex operational environments
Comfort working with UX design, wireframes, data models, and API-driven systems
Technical fluency across autonomy, firmware, and cloud engineering teams
Curiosity and empathy for users managing real-world operational complexity
Why this one is worth a look
Fleet UX is one of the less flashy but more consequential parts of robotics. A drone fleet is only useful if teams can keep aircraft healthy, diagnose problems quickly, and trust the service loop. This role sits in that operational layer.

Shape Skydio's fleet management and internal tooling for drone operations, service, repair, and support workflows.
What the role actually is
Skydio is hiring a senior product manager for Fleet Management and Internal Tools on the Skydio Cloud platform. The role spans customer-facing fleet software and the internal systems that support drone operations, service, repair, troubleshooting, and customer experience.
The job is about making autonomous drone fleets easier to operate at scale. That means turning telemetry, support data, fragmented service workflows, and field feedback into a coherent product roadmap.
What you would work on
Own fleet management and internal tooling roadmaps across device health, inventory, administration, support, service, and repair
Define dock service workflows from issue detection and remote diagnosis through dispatch, parts, verification, and closure
Prototype and validate workflows that simplify operational complexity for customers
Coordinate product work across cloud, UX, hardware, firmware, operations, support, and go-to-market teams

Product experience shipping software for fleet, logistics, mobility, or similarly complex operational environments
Comfort working with UX design, wireframes, data models, and API-driven systems
Technical fluency across autonomy, firmware, and cloud engineering teams
Curiosity and empathy for users managing real-world operational complexity
Why this one is worth a look
Fleet UX is one of the less flashy but more consequential parts of robotics. A drone fleet is only useful if teams can keep aircraft healthy, diagnose problems quickly, and trust the service loop. This role sits in that operational layer.

Senior Product Manager, Hardware Platform
Own product direction for Apptronik's fielded humanoid hardware platform, balancing customer outcomes and engineering constraints.
What the role actually is
Apptronik is hiring a senior product manager for the hardware platform behind its humanoid robot. The role manages the platform as a complete product, using customer outcomes, field data, and engineering constraints to decide what the robot should become next.
This is not pure hardware program management. It is product work around a physical system already moving into field use, where customer value depends on how hardware, software, safety, and operations come together.
What you would work on
Own the roadmap for Apptronik's humanoid hardware platform
Translate field data and customer outcomes into product priorities
Balance engineering tradeoffs, platform maturity, and commercial value
Work across hardware, software, manufacturing, operations, and customer-facing teams
What they are asking for
Product management experience with robotics, hardware platforms, or complex technical products
Ability to connect field evidence with roadmap decisions
Comfort working across engineering, operations, commercialization, and customers
Strong judgment about platform tradeoffs across the product lifecycle
Why this one is worth a look
The useful question for humanoids is no longer just whether the robot can work in a demo. It is which platform choices make the system more valuable and reliable in the field, and this role owns that translation.

text:
Senior Product Manager, Perception and Navigation — Apptronik — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
Product
Senior Product Manager, Perception and Navigation
Own Apollo's perception and navigation roadmap, from field metrics to release gates for scene understanding.
What the role actually is
Apptronik is hiring a senior product manager for perception and navigation on Apollo. The role owns roadmap, scope, sequencing, and field-readiness decisions across detection, tracking, localization, mapping, and obstacle avoidance.
This is a product role for a core autonomy layer. The work is about turning sensor data, customer needs, field failures, and safety constraints into concrete software priorities for a humanoid robot.
What you would work on
Own the roadmap for Apollo's perception and navigation software
Define evaluation metrics, field-test regimes, and release criteria
Shape requirements for perception data collection, labeling, and deployment feedback loops
Partner with sensing, compute, autonomy, UX, industrial design, and product marketing teams
What they are asking for
Product management experience with perception, navigation, autonomy, or similarly technical software
Ability to translate customer and field insights into executable product requirements
Comfort defining metrics for detection, tracking, localization, mapping, latency, and regression risk
Practical judgment about safety, failure modes, validation coverage, and on-robot compute limits
Why this one is worth a look
Perception and navigation are where humanoid promises meet messy physical reality. This role is interesting because it asks a product manager to own not just features, but the release discipline that decides when robot understanding is good enough to trust in the field.

Senior Product Manager, Perception and Navigation
Own the product roadmap for perception and navigation software on Apptronik's humanoid robot platform.
What the role actually is
Apptronik is hiring a senior product manager in Sunnyvale for the perception and navigation layer of Apollo. The role translates robot sensing, scene understanding, localization, mapping, and obstacle-avoidance needs into product priorities and release criteria.
This is a product seat close to autonomy: it owns the roadmap, evaluation metrics, data pipeline requirements, and cross-functional tradeoffs that decide how a humanoid perceives and moves through customer environments.
What you would work on
Set feature priorities for perception, localization, mapping, tracking, and obstacle avoidance
Define field-test and evaluation metrics for robot perception and navigation releases
Turn customer and deployment needs into product requirements for autonomy teams
Partner across sensing, compute, AI, hardware, and go-to-market teams
What they are asking for
Product management experience with robotics, autonomy, AI, or complex hardware-software systems
Ability to reason about robot safety, field validation, and release gates
Comfort translating technical autonomy constraints into customer-facing product tradeoffs
Cross-functional leadership with engineering, data, operations, and commercial teams
Why this one is worth a look
Humanoid roadmaps can get abstract quickly, but perception and navigation are where useful behavior becomes concrete. This role is interesting because it sits between market promises and the measurable reality of what Apollo can safely perceive, decide, and do.

Senior Product Manager, Perception and World Understanding Skills
Lead Digit's perception and learned-capability roadmap, from customer workflows through production readiness metrics.
What the role actually is
Agility Robotics is hiring a senior product manager for Digit's perception, world understanding, and learned robot capabilities. The role turns warehouse and manufacturing workflows into product requirements for what the humanoid needs to perceive, understand, evaluate, and safely deploy.
This is a technical product role, not a generic roadmap job. The person would work with perception, ML, autonomy, simulation, and field teams to decide what capabilities matter, how progress is measured, and when a capability is mature enough for production use.
What you would work on
Own the roadmap for perception-enabled and learned capabilities across Digit's application portfolio
Translate customer tasks into requirements for scene understanding, object understanding, adaptation, motion planning, and learned behaviors
Define product-level metrics for accuracy, robustness, latency, generalization, failure behavior, and operational performance
Coordinate dependencies across robot software, task skills, simulation, infrastructure, hardware, and deployment systems
Shape longer-term robot intelligence strategy around reusable capabilities, not only one-off task implementations
What they are asking for
Product leadership experience in robotics, autonomous systems, AI/ML, computer vision, or another deeply technical product area
Strong working knowledge of machine learning, perception, robotics, autonomy, or related technical domains
Experience translating ambiguous customer needs into measurable technical capability requirements
Comfort working with engineering and research teams on evaluation frameworks, benchmarks, and production-readiness tradeoffs
Why this one is worth a look
This is one of the cleaner product roles for someone who wants to work on the behavior layer of humanoid robotics. Agility is asking for a PM who can connect customer value to perception and learned capabilities, which is exactly where deployed humanoids either become useful products or stay impressive demos.

Senior Product Manager, Sensing and Compute
Drive product strategy for the sensing and compute stack that lets Apptronik's Apollo humanoid perceive and act.
What the role actually is
Apptronik is hiring a senior technical product manager for sensing and compute. The role sits at the hardware/software boundary, turning market demands and user needs into roadmaps for the perception and compute capabilities that support Apollo.
For a humanoid robot, sensing and compute are not invisible infrastructure. They decide what the robot can understand, how reliably it can operate, and where customer expectations meet technical reality.
What you would work on
Define product direction for Apollo's sensing and compute capabilities
Translate customer needs into user-oriented technical roadmaps
Coordinate across hardware, software, AI, safety, and platform teams
Prioritize capability tradeoffs that affect field performance and usability
What they are asking for
Technical product management experience for robotics, AI, hardware, or platform products
Ability to bridge customer needs with sensing, compute, and software constraints
Comfort working with highly technical engineering teams
Strong roadmap judgment for complex systems with field-deployment pressure
Why this one is worth a look
Sensing and compute are where humanoid promises become operational limits. This role is interesting because it requires product judgment about capabilities that users may never name directly but will feel immediately when the robot succeeds or fails.

What the role actually is
Apptronik is hiring a senior product manager for simulation. The role focuses on the product vision and execution path for simulation capabilities used to develop, test, and validate Apollo across the hardware/software divide.
Simulation is becoming one of the most important product surfaces inside robotics companies. The users may be internal engineering and deployment teams, but the decisions shape how fast the robot can learn, regress, recover, and ship safely.
What you would work on
Define product vision and roadmap for Apptronik's simulation capabilities
Translate market, user, and engineering needs into executable simulation priorities
Partner with AI, robotics, software, hardware, and field teams
Shape workflows for testing, validation, and development of humanoid behavior
What they are asking for
Technical product management experience with simulation, robotics, AI, or developer platforms
Ability to work across hardware and software constraints
Comfort turning ambiguous internal needs into product requirements
Strong understanding of how simulation supports deployment readiness
Why this one is worth a look
Robotics simulation is no longer only an engineering utility. It is part of how companies decide what is ready for the real world, which makes this a product role at the center of humanoid deployment risk.

Senior Product Manager, Simulation
Own product direction for simulation workflows that help Apptronik develop, test, and validate Apollo.
What the role actually is
Apptronik is hiring a senior product manager for simulation. The role focuses on the product vision and execution path for simulation capabilities used to develop, test, and validate Apollo across the hardware/software divide.
Simulation is becoming one of the most important product surfaces inside robotics companies. The users may be internal engineering and deployment teams, but the decisions shape how fast the robot can learn, regress, recover, and ship safely.
What you would work on
Define product vision and roadmap for Apptronik's simulation capabilities
Translate market, user, and engineering needs into executable simulation priorities
Partner with AI, robotics, software, hardware, and field teams
Shape workflows for testing, validation, and development of humanoid behavior
What they are asking for
Technical product management experience with simulation, robotics, AI, or developer platforms
Ability to work across hardware and software constraints
Comfort turning ambiguous internal needs into product requirements
Strong understanding of how simulation supports deployment readiness
Why this one is worth a look
Robotics simulation is no longer only an engineering utility. It is part of how companies decide what is ready for the real world, which makes this a product role at the center of humanoid deployment risk.

What the role actually is
Apptronik is hiring a senior product manager to own teleoperation for Apollo. The product serves both internal data collection and customers trying to improve fleet performance, so the role spans operator experience, data throughput, interface quality, and safety.
The listing calls out VR or XR experience and human factors, which makes this more than a backlog-management role. The product surface is the place where a human operator, a robot body, and an autonomy data pipeline meet.
What you would work on
Own the teleoperation product roadmap and release priorities
Define operator interfaces for teleoperated data collection and customer fleet support
Balance data throughput, data quality, operator comfort, and safety
Translate market needs into product requirements across the hardware/software divide

Product management experience for technical, robotics, XR, or hardware/software products
Human factors or operator-workflow sensibility
Ability to define product vision and execute across engineering, design, and customer teams

Why this one is worth a look
Teleoperation is one of the hidden product surfaces in humanoid robotics. It shapes training data, customer support, and what the autonomy team can learn from the field. This role is compelling because operator experience directly affects the robot's learning loop.

Senior Program Manager, Compliance Reporting

What the role actually is
Nuro is hiring a senior program manager for compliance reporting inside the Commercialization and Evaluation function within Software Operations. The role turns regulatory, legal, safety, and operational requirements into reliable reporting programs.
This is a product-adjacent operations role for autonomy: it makes sure external obligations are met with accurate data, clear processes, and documentation that can stand up to review.
What you would work on
Own regulatory reporting programs from requirements gathering through submission and follow-up
Partner with legal, public trust, safety, data platform, and software operations teams
Build review processes, quality controls, documentation, and audit trails for reporting work
Translate technical and operational realities into clear reporting plans and stakeholder updates
What they are asking for
Program management experience in a regulated, compliance-heavy, or public-sector-adjacent environment
Strong writing, editing, and documentation skills under deadline pressure
Ability to work with legal, regulatory, safety, and software operations stakeholders
Independent judgment for managing multiple workstreams with external timelines
Why this one is worth a look
Autonomy companies do not scale on model performance alone. Regulatory reporting is part of the operating system around deployed autonomous vehicles, and this role sits in the machinery that helps Nuro stay credible with regulators, partners, and internal safety teams.

Strong cross-functional judgment across multiple software teams

Senior Reinforcement Learning Engineer
Lead senior-level reinforcement learning work for Apollo humanoid movement and manipulation in Austin.
What the role actually is
Apptronik is hiring a senior reinforcement learning engineer in Austin. The role focuses on applying RL to locomotion and manipulation challenges for humanoid robots, with an explicit expectation that results reach physical hardware.
This is a senior individual-contributor role with mentoring responsibilities, not a generic research label attached to a software job.
What you would work on
Implement and iterate on RL methods for humanoid robot behavior
Transfer policies from simulation to physical robot tests
Improve training infrastructure for high-throughput experimentation
Mentor engineers working on robot-learning systems
What they are asking for
Deep reinforcement learning experience in robotics or embodied systems
Ability to debug model behavior across simulation and hardware
Strong technical judgment around training pipelines and evaluation
Experience guiding other engineers without losing hands-on velocity
Why this one is worth a look
Senior robot-learning roles are valuable when they still stay close to the robot. Apptronik's posting frames the job around actual locomotion and manipulation results, which is the right center of gravity for a humanoid RL role.

Senior Robotics Research Engineer

What the role actually is
Ambi Robotics is hiring a senior robotics research engineer in Berkeley. The role focuses on new technology for Ambi's industrial robot products, including AI-driven robot skills, core robotics libraries, perception, motion planning, and evaluation.
The posting is hands-on research engineering tied to production robotic systems. It is especially relevant because Ambi's systems already operate in logistics environments where robot behavior has to be useful, measurable, and deployable.
What you would work on
Develop new robot applications and capabilities across controls, planning, and perception
Lead R&D projects for AI-driven robot skills powered by foundation models
Contribute to core robotics libraries, training systems, algorithms, and evaluation tooling
Support deployment of new capabilities to production warehouse robots
What they are asking for
Robotics software depth across planning, perception, machine learning, or controls
Strong C++, Python, Linux, Git, and Docker fluency
Experience with commercial robotics systems, motion planning, or computer vision
Ability to lead research projects while staying close to product deployment
Why this one is worth a look
Warehouse automation is a practical testbed for robot learning: tasks are repetitive, but the real world still refuses to be perfectly tidy. Ambi's role is compelling because it asks research to survive contact with deployed parcel-handling systems.

title: Senior Staff Data Scientist, Robotics — Agility — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
text:
Senior Staff Data Scientist, Robotics — Agility — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
User Research
Senior Staff Data Scientist, Robotics
Turn Digit fleet telemetry into reliability models, deployment signals, and product decisions.
What the role actually is
Agility is hiring a senior staff data scientist to define how Digit fleet data becomes reliability insight, product prioritization, and deployment economics. The listing focuses on telemetry, logs, sensor streams, maintenance events, predictive models, and decision systems for a Robots-as-a-Service business.
The role is newly created and explicitly tied to robot performance at scale. It spans predictive maintenance, anomaly detection, manufacturing feedback loops, fleet A/B testing, and the instrumentation needed to measure real-world robot behavior.
What you would work on
Build predictive maintenance and remaining-useful-life models for robot components
Analyze fleet telemetry to connect software versions, site conditions, and usage patterns with intervention rates
Define golden signals for RaaS deployments with product and operations teams
Create anomaly detection, root-cause tooling, and manufacturing-to-field feedback loops
What they are asking for
Senior data science or statistical modeling experience on ambiguous real-world systems
Background in robotics, autonomous systems, hardware, IoT, industrial, or manufacturing environments
Expertise in reliability analysis, time series, anomaly detection, predictive maintenance, or causal inference
Strong production Python and comfort translating messy operational data into decisions
Why this one is worth a look
Fleet telemetry is where deployed robots start teaching the company what actually works. This role belongs on the board because it turns real humanoid operations into the measurements that shape reliability, product roadmap, and customer economics.

Agility
U.S. humanoid robotics company behind Digit and Arc, focused on deployed warehouse and manufacturing automation.

Senior Staff Designer — Shield AI — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
Design and UX
Senior Staff Designer
Lead integrated brand and campaign design systems for Shield AI's autonomy and aircraft product story.
What the role actually is
Shield AI is hiring a senior staff designer to lead integrated brand campaigns across digital, social, events, presentations, advertising, and other touchpoints. The role works with brand, creative, writing, video, marketing, and external partners to turn campaign strategy into visual systems.
For this board, the relevance is not just the word "designer." Shield AI sells autonomy software, autonomous aircraft, and simulation products, so the role is about making complex defense and robotics technology coherent across high-visibility market-facing work.
What you would work on
Translate campaign strategy and creative briefs into visual concepts and scalable systems
Lead high-visibility design work from early exploration through production and launch
Shape briefs, establish visual direction, and turn approved concepts into repeatable systems
Guide other designers, agencies, and production partners so campaigns stay cohesive
Collaborate with writers, video teams, marketers, and external partners
What they are asking for
Senior-level visual design experience with integrated brand campaigns
Strong typography, composition, color, imagery, and art-direction craft
Ability to build scalable visual systems from strategy and creative briefs
Judgment for presenting, defending, and iterating design under demanding timelines
Experience working across digital, social, events, presentations, advertising, and campaign production
Why this one is worth a look
The robotics and autonomy market is crowded with technical claims that blur together quickly. This role is worth noting because it puts a senior designer close to the problem of making Shield AI's autonomy story legible, credible, and consistent across the channels where customers and partners first encounter it.

title: Senior/Staff Machine Learning Engineer, Sensor Simulation — Nuro — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
text:
Senior/Staff Machine Learning Engineer, Sensor Simulation — Nuro — The Robot Age — The Robot Age
User Research
Senior/Staff Machine Learning Engineer, Sensor Simulation
Develop synthetic sensor simulation methods for testing and improving Nuro's autonomy stack.
What the role actually is
Nuro is hiring a senior or staff ML engineer to build synthetic sensor simulation for autonomous driving. The listing focuses on methods that generate realistic camera, lidar, or radar data and then measure whether that simulated data improves autonomy performance.
The role sits between sensor modeling, modern ML graphics, evaluation, and production autonomy. Nuro explicitly mentions NeRF, Gaussian splatting, generative models, and real sensor noise as relevant areas.
What you would work on
Research and implement synthetic sensor simulation methods
Characterize the realism and utility of generated sensor data
Answer evaluation questions about how sensor data affects autonomy performance
Collaborate with autonomy, infrastructure, and systems teams on simulation needs
What they are asking for
ML, robotics, computer science, or electrical engineering background
Hands-on experience training and evaluating modern ML models
Strong Python skills and experience with deep learning frameworks
Experience with sensor modeling, 3D geometry, generative methods, or ML pipelines is a plus
Why this one is worth a look
Simulation quality is becoming a product constraint for autonomy teams. This role is interesting because it is not just building synthetic scenes; it is about whether simulated sensors actually help a robot learn, validate, and ship safer behavior.
